requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Requiring the collected bones of a once-living creature, this spell raises a blue-white bonfire visible for miles across the Underworld. Any ghost who peers into the flame within the following hour sees clearly through their Fetters, without needing to spend an Arcanos to do so.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 121 (PDF 122), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Death Flies Two Sails
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; raises a small sunken ghost ship crewed by a bound ghost figurehead-singer, functioning as a fast courier vessel that boils away in direct sunlight.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer raises a small sunken vessel as a ghost ship, comfortably carrying two passengers (five with effort), with a bound ghost singer serving as its figurehead. The ship functions as a fast courier vessel (see Savage Seas) with 8L soak and 16 health levels, and boils away at a rate of one health level per turn if caught in direct sunlight.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 121 (PDF 122), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Funerary Misted Vessel
summary: Labyrinth Circle version of Death Flies Two Sails; raises a much larger fog-shrouded ghost ship built to marine-assault-trireme specifications, capable of stealthy troop transport.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Labyrinth Circle version of Death Flies Two Sails raises a much larger ghost ship comfortably carrying twenty passengers (fifty uncomfortably, or eighty walking dead), shrouded in a stealth-granting fog bank. It functions as a marine assault trireme with 14L soak and 16-32 health levels depending on configuration.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 121 (PDF 122), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Death Inversion Loop
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; forces a ghost to relive her death in a paralyzed loop via a contested Willpower and Essence duel, draining permanent Willpower with every loss until the ghost is freed or reduced to a mindless haunt of the death scene.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The target ghost relives the moment of her death, paralyzed, in a contested Willpower + Essence duel against the necromancer. The ghost loses one dot of permanent Willpower for every loop she loses, and is freed only if she wins the contest outright; a ghost reduced to zero permanent Willpower this way becomes a mindless haunt bound to the scene of her death. The spell can also be cast on a living creature to force a disturbing vision of their own death, imposing a one-die penalty for the rest of that turn; casting it against a target too strong for the necromancer to safely punish can rebound on the caster instead.
compatibility: Target: One ghost (or one living creature).
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 122 (PDF 123), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Death Mask
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell requiring a living sacrifice on first casting; disguises the necromancer as an ordinary ghost using a regenerating shroud of Elsewhere-drawn corpus that absorbs damage before the caster takes any.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell requires a living sacrifice the first time it is ever cast. It cloaks the necromancer in a disguising shroud drawn from Elsewhere, making her appear to be an ordinary ghost. Seeing through the disguise requires the necromancer's Essence + Craft (Moliation) to be beaten by the viewer's Perception + Awareness; mortals and other living creatures cannot see through it at all. The ghostly shroud absorbs damage before the caster does, regenerating one health level per week while in Elsewhere; if the shroud is destroyed it must be regrown before the spell can be used again.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 123 (PDF 124), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Drawing Blind Edge
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; permanently destroys a ghost by drawing its corpus into a translucent reaver-daiklave-like blade, distributing the drained Essence among the weapon's stats.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer draws the target ghost's corpus into a translucent blade resembling a reaver daiklave: it deals half damage to the living, aggravated damage to ghosts and spirits, and permanently destroys the source ghost, draining its Essence into the weapon. The necromancer distributes one point per point of the ghost's permanent Essence among the weapon's Speed, Accuracy, Damage, and Defense, with no single stat exceeding the reaver daiklave's normal caps. The weapon persists until dismissed, dispelled by countermagic, or until dawn.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 124 (PDF 125), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Dusk Eyes
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; grants sight across the life/death boundary, letting the caster see into the Underworld from Creation or vice versa, one world at a time.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: For an hour (as measured by the Calendar of Setesh), the necromancer can see across the boundary between life and death, viewing the Underworld while standing in Creation or Creation while standing in the Underworld. She can only perceive one world at a time, and suffers a two-success penalty if she tries to act on what she sees in the world she is not physically present in while otherwise blind to her actual surroundings. The spell grants no benefit while already standing within a shadowland.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 124 (PDF 125), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Easing the Forsaken Memory
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; permanently erases a single haunt (a place tainted by a lingering death-memory), or relocates it for an additional mote per mile of distance.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell permanently erases a single haunt of the necromancer's choosing. For an additional cost of one mote per mile, the necromancer may instead relocate the haunt to a location of her choosing rather than erasing it outright.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 124 (PDF 125), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Congealing the Last Thought
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell related to Easing the Forsaken Memory; creates a new haunt from a cooperating ghost's memory or from the necromancer's own imagination, lasting far longer if created in the Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This related spell creates a haunt out of whole cloth, either drawn from a cooperating ghost's mind or invented entirely from the necromancer's own imagination. Haunts created in Creation last one month per point of the caster's permanent Essence; haunts created in the Underworld are effectively permanent.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 124 (PDF 125), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Emperor's Chains
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; either halves the movement rate and doubles movement-Arcanoi costs for every ghost within fifty yards, or renders a single nearby ghost immobile with tripled movement-Arcanoi costs.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: As the necromancer claps her hands, every ghost within fifty yards finds its movement rate halved and the Essence cost of any movement-related Arcanoi doubled. Alternatively, the necromancer may focus the spell's effect on a single ghost within twenty yards, rendering that ghost completely unable to move under its own power and tripling the Essence cost of any movement-enhancing Arcanoi it tries to use.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 125 (PDF 126), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Faces of the Dead
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; creates a silver twelve-faced mace that captures the faces of ghosts it strikes hard enough, later collapsing into a jar that imprisons the captured souls.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer creates a silver mace with a twelve-faced head. Any blow that deals damage equal to or greater than a struck ghost's permanent Essence captures that ghost's face on the weapon in a flash of blue light. After an hour the weapon dissolves into a jar (12L/12B soak, 20 health levels) holding all of the trapped ghosts, who are freed only if the jar shatters, at which point they are left drained of Essence. Abyssals commonly use this spell to collect souls for forging into soulsteel.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 125 (PDF 126), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Field of Fell Dreams
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; raises skeletal hands from the ground across an area that grasp and hold, but do not harm, anyone who passes through until the spell ends at midnight.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Skeletal hands burst from the ground or stone across the area of effect and attempt to clinch anyone who moves through, using a seven-die pool for each clinch attempt; the hands never try to inflict damage, only to hold their victims in place. The hands have effectively no soak and are fragile, but a new hand replaces each one destroyed. Anyone caught must spend a mote of Essence to become material if they were not already. The spell's effect ends at midnight, as measured by the Calendar of Setesh.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 125 (PDF 126), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Five Gifts
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; grants a ghost a taste of the sensations of life, restoring temporary Willpower equal to the successes rolled on its highest Virtue, at risk of the ghost craving the pleasure again over time.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The target ghost briefly experiences the world as it did in life, its dulled senses restored to vivid intensity. The ghost gains temporary Willpower equal to the successes rolled on its highest-rated Virtue, which may temporarily exceed its normal maximum. This can raise a ghost's Temperance-tested resolve to peacefully let go of mortal pleasure; when the spell ends, the ghost rolls Temperance, and failure costs it a single point of temporary Willpower, with any excess Willpower above the normal maximum vanishing along with the spell's effects. The spell lasts only until the next sunset, but repeated use can leave ghosts yearning for it, growing more pliable or even slavish to obtain it again.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 125 (PDF 126), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Flesh and Bone Winds
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; surrounds the caster with a growing storm of shattered bone and flesh that shreds anyone stepping into it and imposes accuracy penalties on attacks against the necromancer.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The ground around the necromancer erupts, tearing free shattered bone and soft ribbons of flesh that spin around the caster at ever-increasing speed, starting at a one-yard radius and growing as it absorbs more corpses, up to twice the caster's Essence in radius. The storm imposes a one-die accuracy penalty on melee attacks and a three-die penalty on ranged attacks made against the necromancer, and deals three dice of lethal damage per turn to anyone who steps into it. Creatures slain by the storm are shredded, adding their substance to its fury and radius.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 126 (PDF 127), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Flesh-Sloughing Wave
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; hurls a ball of ivory Essence that strips flesh from bone across a radius, useful both as an attack and as a utility spell for harvesting materials for undead war-machine construction.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer hurls a ball of ivory Essence that bursts, stripping flesh from bone in a radius equal to five times her Essence in yards. Living creatures in the area suffer lethal damage soaked at twice their Occult rating (or lose their flesh outright), making the spell equally useful as a weapon or as a utility spell for harvesting materiel to construct undead war machines. A Fair One killed by this spell dies in a blinding flash of light.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 127 (PDF 128), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Gathering a Ghost's Strings
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; instantly learns a ghost's Fetters and Passions, or for an additional ten motes overwrites them with the necromancer's own design for up to a month per point of permanent Essence spent.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Over the course of a full turn, the necromancer instantly learns a target ghost's Fetters and Passions. For an additional cost of ten motes, she may instead overwrite those Fetters and Passions with a new design of her own choosing; the overwritten values fade back to normal after one month per point of the necromancer's permanent Essence. Ghost-blooded targets are immune to the overwrite effect unless they possess a Merit that removes that protection. The Celestial sorcery version of this spell costs twenty motes and takes ten minutes to cast.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 127 (PDF 128), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Puzzle Box of Love
summary: Labyrinth Circle version of Gathering a Ghost's Strings; permanently rearranges a ghost's Passions and Fetters entirely, contestable only once a year on the anniversary of the ghost's death.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Labyrinth Circle version of Gathering a Ghost's Strings permanently and entirely rearranges a target ghost's Passions and Fetters according to the necromancer's design. The ghost may only contest this rearrangement once per year, on the anniversary of its death.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 127 (PDF 128), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Gentle Call of Lethe
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; marks a living target so that, upon death, they are barred from becoming a ghost, instead passing to Lethe or Oblivion depending on their temperament, and is incompatible with Rune of Sweet Passing.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer marks a living target. Should that creature later die, it is barred from ever becoming a ghost, instead passing on to Lethe or to Oblivion depending on its temperament at the moment of death. This spell cannot be cast on a target already affected by Rune of Sweet Passing, and vice versa.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 128 (PDF 129), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Master Puppeteer's Knife
summary: Shadowlands Circle countermagic-like spell; instantly destroys every animated-dead extra created by Raise the Skeletal Horde or Arisen Legion within a ninety-degree arc, and can destroy Exquisite Undead Aide-created undead one at a time, but cannot affect undead war machines.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell functions much like countermagic, instantly destroying every animated-dead extra created by Raise the Skeletal Horde or Arisen Legion within a ninety-degree arc out to ten yards. It can also destroy Exquisite Undead Aide-created undead servants, though only one at a time, and it has no effect whatsoever on undead war machines.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 128 (PDF 129), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Midnight Shadow Sun
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; cast on a shadowland border, forces creatures crossing it to emerge on the caster's chosen side for the next five minutes.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Cast upon a shadowland's border, this spell forces up to twice the caster's Essence in creatures who cross that border to emerge on whichever side the necromancer chooses, for the next five minutes.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 128 (PDF 129), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Folding Midnight
summary: Void Circle version of Midnight Shadow Sun; permanently curses a shadowland border to function as a one-way portal in a single direction, requiring the necromancer to walk its perimeter at the proper time of day.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Void Circle version of Midnight Shadow Sun permanently curses a shadowland's border to become a one-way portal that only permits crossing in a single direction. Casting it requires the necromancer to walk the entire perimeter of the shadowland at the time of day appropriate to her desired effect; an unlucky ghost or other creature caught by it may find itself permanently unable to return to the side it started from.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 128 (PDF 129), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Mother Darkness
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; reshapes a one-mile radius into a somber, threatening environment that puts Underworld denizens more at ease and counts toward an Abyssal shedding Resonance, but cannot be cast on a Demesne.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Over the course of a minute, the necromancer reshapes the local environment within a one-mile radius, darkening the sky, graying the flora and fauna, and adding an air of menace. Creatures of the Underworld find themselves more at ease within the area, recovering an extra mote of Essence per day spent there, and the spell is considered a significant fraction of the trappings of death an Abyssal needs to shed Resonance. The area cannot be cast upon a Demesne, and when cast on Wyld terrain it reduces the Wyld's strength by one tier while its effects persist. The transformation settles in over the course of a week and fades over a similar span once the spell ends.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 129 (PDF 130), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Piercing the Heel
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; using a ghost's former body as an arcane link, ritually pierces its heels with iron nails to bind the ghost from ever physically harming the necromancer, making it fall lame if it tries.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell cannot be cast unless the necromancer has access to her victim's former body, which serves as the arcane link. Ritually piercing the body's heel tendons with iron nails while speaking the ghost's name binds the ghost so that it cannot enact any physical harm upon the necromancer; should it ever attempt to do so, it immediately falls lame and unable to move until it abandons the intention. The binding may be broken by countermagic cast on the ghost, by removing the iron nails from the body's heels, or automatically if the body decays too far for the nails to be removed at all.
compatibility: Target: One ghost. Requires an arcane link.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 129 (PDF 130), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Ringing Hun Rebuke
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; pulls two iron rings from thin air and claps them to resonate for an hour, making ghosts reluctant to approach within five yards or to strike the caster.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer pulls two iron rings out of thin air, wears one on the middle finger of each hand, and claps her hands to make the rings resonate for the following hour. While the rings sound, any ghost must succeed at a Willpower roll (difficulty 3) to approach within five yards of the caster, and finds it abhorrent to strike her, granting the necromancer an effective additional soak of 2L/3B against ghostly attacks; ranged attacks from beyond the five-yard radius are unaffected. Ghosts in a crowd instinctively move out of the necromancer's path while the spell is active, though a sufficiently motivated and numerous mob can still shove past. There is a greater Labyrinth Circle version of this spell called Brick-by-Brick Solitude.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 129 (PDF 130), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Brick-by-Brick Solitude
summary: Labyrinth Circle version of Ringing Hun Rebuke; surrounds the necromancer with an expanding cylinder of arcane symbols that ghosts cannot pierce or make hand-to-hand attacks through.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Labyrinth Circle version of Ringing Hun Rebuke summons several dozen arcane symbols in a cylinder around the necromancer that, if cast under direct sunlight, expand rapidly to a radius equal to ten times the caster's permanent Essence in yards. Ghosts cannot pierce this invisible boundary and therefore cannot make hand-to-hand attacks through it, though ranged attacks still function normally once they cross into range; the boundary moves with the necromancer and can shove most ghosts out of the way with a Strength rating three times the necromancer's own, though a sufficiently large and determined mob can still resist being pushed. The book does not restate an explicit Essence cost for this version; treat it as at least as costly as the base spell's 19 motes pending clarification. [FLAG: the sourcebook describes this variant in prose immediately following Ringing Hun Rebuke without a separate 'Cost:' header; the cost was not printed and should be treated as an open question rather than assumed.]
cost: Not specified (greater version of Ringing Hun Rebuke)
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 129 (PDF 130), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Seat of Deadly Splendors
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; raises a bone throne from the ground granting social bonuses and the ability to see and command dematerialized ghosts to manifest.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Speaking blasphemies to the local gods or ghosts and letting a drop of blood fall upon the earth, the necromancer causes a massive bone throne to burst from the ground for her to sit upon. While seated, she gains a two-die bonus to all rolls involving intimidation, persuasion, or perceiving true motives and lies, and can see dematerialized ghosts as though they were material, forcing any such ghost to manifest at a cost of two motes (adding one to the spell's dice bonuses when applied against ghosts). The magical effects last only an hour, though the throne itself remains until hewn from the ground and removed (treat it as a stone statue, see Exalted, p. 239); destroying the throne ends the spell's magical effects immediately. The spell cannot be successfully cast if the necromancer is on a second floor, in a tree, or otherwise not in contact with the ground.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Shattered Void Mirror
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; briefly inverts a living victim's physical form against a reflection drawn from the Void, dealing lethal damage equal to twice her remaining health levels and draining motes equal to twice her permanent Essence.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer throws her arm out toward a target; for a moment, the colors of the victim's image invert as her Essence is thrown against an exact opposite drawn from the Void. The target's skin and bones crack, her flesh grows cold and pale, and she suffers a number of dice of raw lethal damage equal to twice her current remaining health levels, soakable only by her natural soak, and loses a number of motes of Essence equal to twice her permanent Essence. If the spell kills its target, the victim's inverted image shatters into pieces that scatter on the Underworld's wind, draining her corpse of all color; the spell instantly slays extras.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Silent Master's Pollen
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; conjures a point of gray-white light that lures a ghost toward Lethe, freeing any ghost successfully struck by it of necromantic bindings, with greater Labyrinth and Void versions freeing higher-Essence ghosts and larger groups.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer summons a small, nigh-irresistible point of light representing the cycle of passing through Lethe, which she may either touch directly to a ghost's corpus with a successful unarmed attack or hurl at a target using Wits + Thrown. A ghost struck by the light must roll Willpower (difficulty 3) or silently slip into Lethe with no risk of falling into Oblivion; whether or not the ghost actually passes on, any Charms or spells binding it shatter and release it, provided the bound Arcanoi or Charm was of the Iron Circle or Essence 3 or lower. Greater versions of this spell exist: Black Vial, a Labyrinth Circle spell (24 motes) that frees ghosts bound by Onyx Circle or Essence 4-or-lower effects, and Empty Night Future, a Void Circle spell (32 motes) affecting up to ten ghosts within a ten-yard radius and freeing any bound effect regardless of Essence. For these greater versions, ghosts must beat a higher Willpower roll (difficulty 4 for Black Vial, 5 for Empty Night Future) or be drawn fully into Oblivion instead of Lethe, with the resulting agony absorbed by the caster at a cost of one mote per soul lost this way.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Black Vial
summary: Labyrinth Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen; frees ghosts bound by Onyx Circle Necromancy or Charms of Essence 4 or lower, risking Oblivion instead of Lethe if the target fails its Willpower roll.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Labyrinth Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen frees ghosts bound by Onyx Circle Necromancy or by Charms of Essence 4 or lower. A struck ghost must beat a Willpower roll at difficulty 4 or be drawn into Oblivion instead of Lethe; the necromancer absorbs one mote of agony for each soul lost this way.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Empty Night Future
summary: Void Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen; frees up to ten ghosts within a ten-yard radius from any binding effect regardless of Essence, risking Oblivion instead of Lethe on a failed Willpower roll.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greatest, Void Circle version of Silent Master's Pollen affects up to ten ghosts within a ten-yard radius simultaneously and frees them from any binding effect regardless of its Essence rating. Each struck ghost must beat a Willpower roll at difficulty 5 or be drawn into Oblivion instead of Lethe; the necromancer absorbs one mote of agony for each soul lost this way.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Smoothing the Crease-Worn Mind
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; silences the voices of long-dead gods in a target's mind, relieving Whisper of Oblivion contagion fear, calming spectres regarding Void subservience, and temporarily suppressing an Abyssal's Whispers of the Malfeans channeling ability.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: By touch (an unarmed attack roll at a one-die penalty against an unwilling target), the necromancer silences the voices of long-dead gods that trouble her target's mind. This relieves the fear associated with Whisper of Oblivion contagion (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 284), calms spectres regarding their subservience to the Void, and quiets mortwights and other quiescent undead. If cast on an Abyssal, the target temporarily loses the ability to channel Whispers of the Malfeans. The effect lasts one day per point of the caster's Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 130 (PDF 131), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Stones Worn Smooth
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; a target ghost's heart is pulled from her and crushed into a black-diamond Hearthstone unless she beats a Willpower roll, drawing her toward Lethe or Oblivion until the stone shatters.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The target ghost's player rolls Willpower against a difficulty equal to the necromancer's Essence; on a failure, the ghost's heart is pulled from her corpus and crushed into a black diamond Hearthstone whose level equals the ghost's permanent Essence. The Hearthstone lasts only one day before shattering, cannot be used within Creation, and shatters instantly if exposed to the Unconquered Sun's light. While it persists, the ghost is drawn irresistibly toward Lethe or Oblivion until the Hearthstone breaks.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 131 (PDF 132), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Trolling the Dark Water
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; casts a violet Essence net that settles over the ground and forces ghosts passing through it to spend a mote to manifest, with no effect in the already-material Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer casts a violet net of Essence into the air, which settles over the ground within twenty-five yards. Any ghost passing through the net's area is forced to spend a mote of Essence to manifest if not already material; the necromancer may spend an additional five motes to force manifestation outright rather than merely charging for it. The spell has no effect in the Underworld, where ghosts are already material by default.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 131 (PDF 132), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Without Pity, Without Scorn
summary: Shadowlands Circle spell; a shattering sphere of Void energy renders all of a ghost's Fetters within an area inert for a time based on Fetter rating, or can instead be hurled at a specific ghost to permanently sever it from one chosen Fetter.
requirements: Necromancy: Shadowlands Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: A sphere of Void energy shatters on the ground, rendering any Fetter (a physical representation binding a ghost to the world) within the area of effect inert for a period based on that Fetter's rating: two months for a one-dot Fetter, one month for two dots, two weeks for three dots, six days for four dots, and three days for a five-dot Fetter. Alternatively, the necromancer may instead hurl the sphere at a specific ghost using Dexterity + Thrown to permanently sever that ghost from one chosen Fetter outright.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Shadowlands Circle, p. 131 (PDF 132), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Baneful Sun
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; curses a target with a taint that resonates against Creation, inflicting a slow, eventually lethal drain, or against the Underworld with slow-healing wounds; a reverse version curses targets to wander Creation forever or bars heroes from the Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer curses her target with a taint that resonates against Creation: while in Creation, the victim suffers a one-die penalty to all actions and one unsoakable die of aggravated damage per month, which will eventually kill her if left uncured; while in the Underworld, the target's wounds heal at only one health level per month and never any faster. Casting this against a heroic character requires a contested Essence roll. A reverse version of the spell, Baneful Shadow, instead curses the target to wander Creation forever, unable to regain any Essence, or to be permanently barred from entering the Underworld.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 131 (PDF 132), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Baneful Shadow
summary: Labyrinth Circle reverse version of Baneful Sun; curses a target to wander Creation forever unable to regain Essence, or permanently bars a hero from the Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This reverse version of Baneful Sun curses its target to wander Creation forever, unable to ever regain Essence, or alternatively bars a heroic target from ever entering the Underworld again.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 131 (PDF 132), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Clamoring Shackles
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; fires an unparryable, soak-piercing magical arrow that, if it drops the target below Incapacitated, latches soulsteel grave-prison chains onto a second ghost of the caster's choosing.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer fires a magical arrow using Wits + Archery, dealing lethal damage equal to three times her Occult rating and ignoring any soak bonuses granted by Arcanoi or artifacts. If the arrow reduces its target below Incapacitated, soulsteel grave-prison chains (Artifact rating two) latch onto a second ghost of the necromancer's choosing, binding it. The chains last one day per point of the necromancer's permanent Essence unless she spends six experience points to make them permanent, breakable thereafter only by Obsidian Countermagic. A Void Circle version of this spell, Blackstorm Wagon, rains down arrows across a wide area instead.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 132 (PDF 133), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Blackstorm Wagon
summary: Void Circle version of Clamoring Shackles; a single accuracy roll applies a rain of magical arrows to every target in a hundred-yard radius within five hundred yards, with any ghost slain suffering the same grave-chain fate.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Void Circle version of Clamoring Shackles rains down a barrage of magical arrows: the necromancer makes a single Perception + Archery roll that applies to every target within a hundred-yard radius, out to a range of five hundred yards. Any ghost slain by one of these arrows suffers the same soulsteel grave-prison chain fate as a target of Clamoring Shackles.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 132 (PDF 133), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Crystal Ghost Shard
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; ejects the necromancer's higher soul as a fully functional ghost while her body is protected inside a black crystal shell, letting her act, fight, and learn Arcanoi as a ghost until the shell shatters.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer's higher soul is ejected from her body as a ghost, while her body is encased in a protective black crystal shell (30L/20B soak) that shatters after taking forty levels of damage, at which point it deals two unsoakable levels of aggravated damage to the caster and forcibly pulls her spirit back into her body. While committed, her body is inert and protected; her ghost-self can act freely, use ghost Charms, and learn Arcanoi (at normal cost, or a discount if the necromancer is Moonshadow or Eclipse Caste). If the ejected spirit is slain while outside her body, the necromancer's body loses one dot of permanent Willpower upon her forced return.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 132 (PDF 133), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Dead Man's Voice
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; remotely scries and lightly possesses a victim through an arcane link, letting the necromancer see, hear, and speak through the victim while the victim rapidly decays or ages, restricted to living targets of Essence 1 or ghosts of Essence 2 or lower.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Using an arcane link, the necromancer sees and hears through a victim's senses and can speak through her mouth, though without any motor control over the target's body. While the spell is active, the victim decays or ages rapidly, dying in roughly thirty minutes if mortal (ghosts fare somewhat better, melting away like butter); this spell can only target living creatures of Essence 1 or lower, or ghosts of Essence 2 or lower, and treats extras as having seven health levels for this purpose. The victim suffers one unsoakable level of lethal damage for every five minutes the spell remains active.
compatibility: Target: One creature. Requires an arcane link.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 133 (PDF 134), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Denying the Call
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; temporarily revives a body that died less than a minute ago, restoring it to one health level above Incapacitated and immune to all but aggravated damage for the spell's duration.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell can only be cast on a creature that died less than a minute ago. It temporarily revives the body to one health level above Incapacitated, harmable only by aggravated damage, for a number of turns equal to the necromancer's Essence; it cannot be recast on the same target a second time. When the spell ends, the target dies again, this time at half its normal maximum health levels, in the Underworld. A Void Circle version, Barred Tomb, extends the revival to up to an hour and restores health levels equal to the caster's Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 134 (PDF 135), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Barred Tomb
summary: Void Circle version of Denying the Call; extends the temporary revival to up to an hour, with health levels equal to the caster's Essence.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Void Circle version of Denying the Call extends the temporary revival of a recently dead creature to up to an hour, restoring it with health levels equal to the necromancer's Essence rather than the base spell's fixed level above Incapacitated. [FLAG: an explicit mote cost for this variant was not printed in the passage describing it; treat the cost as at least the base spell's 24 motes pending clarification.]
cost: Not specified (greater version of Denying the Call)
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 134 (PDF 135), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Golden Shadows Cast in Frieze
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; frees a spectre from the Malfeans' whispers and Void obligations, restoring its pre-corruption memories and afterlife through a contested Willpower and Essence roll, and can also strip a pitiable ghost's Arcanoi use.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer attempts to free a spectre from its Malfean whispers and obligations to the Void, restoring its former, pre-corruption memories and afterlife. This requires a contested Willpower + Essence roll against the target at difficulty 7, with the necromancer able to purchase additional successes for three motes each, up to a maximum equal to her own Essence. As an alternative use, the necromancer may strike a pitiable ghost with Wits + Occult against the ghost's dodge to strip its ability to use or learn new Arcanoi until the following midnight, as measured by the Calendar of Setesh. This spell can also cleanse Oblivion's Whisper taint from an affected ghost.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 134 (PDF 135), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Gray Eyes Shield and Shell
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the necromancer's eyes turn gray and dull, granting immunity to ghosts' Arcanoi (including Skinriders' grasp and Essence-theft effects) and to mental influence from ghosts, with self-moliation as the sole exception.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer's eyes turn gray and dull as this spell takes hold, granting her immunity to ghostly Arcanoi: Skinriders cannot grasp her, and Essence-theft effects targeting her simply fail. She is also immune to mental influence originating from ghosts. The only exception to this protection is self-inflicted moliation.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 136 (PDF 137), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Infinite Footsteps
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; creates a shortcut tunnel through the Labyrinth connecting two previously visited or scried points, letting travel between them take exactly one day regardless of true distance.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer creates a shortcut tunnel through the Labyrinth connecting two points she has previously visited or scried. Travel through this tunnel takes exactly one day, regardless of the true distance between the two points, and the tunnel itself lasts a number of days equal to the necromancer's Essence.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 136 (PDF 137), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Joyless Spirit's Corruption
summary: Labyrinth Circle ritual spell; completes a rare and foul spirit's corruption from a life-affirming god into allegiance with the death-gods.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This ritual spell completes the corruption of a god from a life-affirming allegiance into service to the death-gods. It only functions on rare, already-foul spirits already predisposed toward such corruption.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 136 (PDF 137), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Links Born of Tumult
summary: Labyrinth Circle hour-long ritual; splits the necromancer's lower soul off as her own hungry-ghost-like shadow that she can command or directly inhabit, ending only when she devours it and reabsorbs her lower soul.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Over the course of an hour-long ritual, the necromancer splits her lower soul off into a hungry-ghost-like shadow of herself, using the hungry ghost creation rules (see Exalted: The Abyssals, pp. 61-62). The shadow can be given simple commands, or the necromancer may directly inhabit and control it, leaving her own body powerless while she does so. The spell has no fixed duration, ending only when the necromancer devours the shadow and reabsorbs her lower soul. If the shadow is destroyed while separate, the necromancer's lower soul returns to her violently, costing her one point of permanent Willpower; if she was actively controlling the shadow when it was destroyed, she is also stunned for an hour.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 136 (PDF 137), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Rattled Bones of War
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; bones fly from the ground to form a scout- or common-warstrider-scale construct of bone and iron around the caster, complete with a summonable fighting-chain weapon, lasting an hour and extendable at additional cost.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Bones fly up from the ground and assemble into either a scout warstrider or a common warstrider (fully attuned) made of bone and iron around the necromancer. It functions as a normal warstrider of the chosen type, though piercing its armor wounds the pilot's spirit directly. It comes with a summonable Warstrider Fighting Chain weapon (Speed +3, Accuracy -1, Damage +4, Defense +2). The construct lasts one hour, extendable by paying eleven motes per additional hour, and the necromancer collapses when its duration finally ends. A Labyrinth Circle variant, Walking Gore Titan, and a Void Circle variant, Void Cocoon Warrior, produce larger constructs from different materials.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 136 (PDF 137), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Walking Gore Titan
summary: Labyrinth Circle variant of Rattled Bones of War; requires a ritual sacrifice with an obsidian knife of beings whose cumulative permanent Essence totals ten or more, raising a crimson warstrider of pooled blood wielding an entrails fighting chain.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This variant of Rattled Bones of War requires a ritual sacrifice, performed with an obsidian knife, of one or more beings whose cumulative permanent Essence totals ten or more. A crimson warstrider rises from the pooled blood of the sacrifice, wielding an entrails fighting chain in place of the base spell's bone weapon, but otherwise duplicates Rattled Bones of War's construct in all other respects.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 137 (PDF 138), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Void Cocoon Warrior
summary: Void Circle variant of Rattled Bones of War; a black cocoon of nothingness becomes a twenty-foot noble or royal warstrider that can be upgraded with a lethal health level sacrifice, lasting two hours and extendable at additional cost.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This greater, Void Circle variant of Rattled Bones of War forms a black cocoon of nothingness around the necromancer that becomes a twenty-foot mighty noble or royal warstrider. The necromancer may sacrifice a lethal health level to upgrade the construct to a ruddy-red royal warstrider that cannot be healed until the spell ends. It lasts two hours, extendable by paying motes equal to half the spell's original cost per additional hour, and can mount additional Void Cocoon weapons at an extra Essence-based cost.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 137 (PDF 138), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Seven Visions Wisdom
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; captures and binds a lower-Essence ghost into a soulsteel medallion, letting the wearer substitute the ghost's Ability rating for their own at a penalty when using an Ability they lack naturally.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer captures and binds a ghost of lower Essence than her own into a soulsteel medallion (Artifact rating two, commitment cost two motes). The wearer of the medallion may substitute any one of the bound ghost's Ability ratings for her own when performing a relevant task, though she suffers a two-die penalty if using an Ability she does not naturally possess at all. The medallion loses its integrity after being struck by countermagic or after a number of months equal to the necromancer's Essence; she may spend six experience points to make it permanent and immune to everything but Obsidian Countermagic. Wearing multiple such medallions at once causes them to conflict, imposing a two-die penalty on either Ability substituted.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 137 (PDF 138), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Rebirth Into Darkness
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; binds a ghost with an invisible collar that forces it to keep re-manifesting after every death or dissipation rather than passing on or risking Oblivion, commonly used by Deathlords and Abyssals for repeated torture.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer binds a target ghost with an invisible collar that compels it to re-manifest after every subsequent death or dissipation, rather than being allowed to pass on or risk falling into Oblivion. The binding persists until the caster chooses to forfeit it; if the ghost's permanent Essence was 0 when bound, maintaining the binding after each recurrence costs ten motes per instance, but otherwise it renews automatically. This spell is commonly used by Deathlords and Abyssals to inflict repeated torture on a captive ghost.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 138 (PDF 139), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Shadow Stones Travel
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; temporarily converts a portion of Creation into a shadowland overlay that spreads over three turns, mirroring normal shadowland rules for anyone inside, with the inverse effect if cast within the Underworld.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell temporarily converts a portion of Creation into a shadowland, with the overlay spreading to a fifty-yard radius over the course of three turns. The transformed area follows normal shadowland rules for anyone caught within it for a number of turns equal to the necromancer's Essence, or until she dismisses the effect early. If cast within the Underworld instead, the spell has the inverse effect, temporarily revealing a patch of Creation.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 138 (PDF 139), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Shield of Shattering Bones
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; lets the caster reflexively shunt incoming damage onto a marked, nearby animate-dead minion in line of sight, which visibly bears the transferred blow.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: At the time of casting, the necromancer marks a nearby animate-dead minion (such as a skeleton or zombie) within five times her Essence in yards and in line of sight. Thereafter, for a reflexive cost of three motes, she may shunt an incoming attack's damage onto the marked minion instead of suffering it herself; the minion visibly displays the transferred blow, such as a skeleton's ribcage collapsing. The marked minion remains valid until sunrise (within the Underworld) or until the spell is recast to mark a new minion.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 139 (PDF 140), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Silenced Whispered Prayers
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; cuts off a target's incoming worship, dropping a single target's Cult rating to zero for the spell's duration, or halving or reducing all Cult ratings within a wide area if cast on a region instead.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Cast on a single target, this spell drops that target's Cult rating (Underworld or Ancestor) to zero for the spell's duration. Cast instead on an area (a forty-five-yard radius), it reduces every ghost's Cult rating within the area by one dot, and halves (rounding down) the Cult rating of living creatures within it. The spell's effect lasts until the Underworld's sun has risen seven times.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 139 (PDF 140), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Sweet Voice Familiar
summary: Labyrinth Circle spell; the caster's body goes slack and possessed, broadcasting maddening Whispers of Oblivion to every ghost within miles equal to her Essence, risking a taint effect on ghosts who fail a Willpower roll and draining temporary Willpower from mortals who hear it.
requirements: Necromancy: Labyrinth Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer's body goes slack, possessed by the spell, and broadcasts maddening Whispers of Oblivion to every ghost within a number of miles equal to her Essence. Affected ghosts must beat a Willpower roll at a difficulty equal to the caster's Whispers rating plus five, or become poisoned by the promises of Oblivion (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 284 sidebar). Mortals who hear the broadcast must roll Willpower against the caster's Whispers rating, losing temporary Willpower equal to their margin of failure.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Labyrinth Circle, p. 139 (PDF 140), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Birth of Sanity's Sorrow
summary: Void Circle spell, castable only once per lifetime in the instant before death and taught directly by a Malfean; transforms the caster into a unique hungry-ghost-like combat form for one scene before she irrevocably dies, her soul devoured by the Void.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This spell can only be cast once per lifetime, and only in the instant before the necromancer's death, having been taught to her directly by a Malfean. It transforms her into a unique hungry-ghost-like combat form, using the hungry ghost rules (see Exalted: The Abyssals, pp. 61-62) with her Essence added to her Strength and Stamina, and a number of health levels equal to five times her Essence plus an Incapacitated level. Charms cost only one mote each to invoke in this form, and a single mote can substitute for a point of Willpower. The form comes with three unique, bespoke powers costing five to ten motes each, devised jointly by the Storyteller and player. The form remains active for one scene, after which the necromancer instantly and irrevocably dies, her soul devoured by the Void — unless she was already Incapacitated at the moment of casting, in which case she instead survives at the Incapacitated health level. [NOTE: this is a capstone, character-ending transformation spell rather than a standard combat spell, and its bespoke powers are explicitly GM/player-collaborative content rather than fixed mechanics.]
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 139 (PDF 140), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Black Faith
summary: Void Circle desperate-suicide ritual; the caster sacrifices a ghost to the Abyss after a half-hour of worship, then leaps into the Void, either being teleported anywhere by the pleased Malfeans or destroyed permanently if they are unimpressed.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: In this desperate ritual, the necromancer sacrifices a ghost's pain and corpus to the Abyss after a half-hour of dedicated worship, then leaps bodily into the Void. If the Malfeans are pleased with the offering, they revoke her intended dissolution and instead teleport her anywhere she wishes — the Labyrinth, the Underworld, or Creation — bypassing all wards along the way. If they are unimpressed, she is instead destroyed, permanently and without recourse. This spell's outcome is explicitly Storyteller-adjudicated and should be used in close coordination with the Storyteller.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 140 (PDF 141), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: The Clay of Warped Dreams
summary: Void Circle spell; requires sacrificing three ghosts after a ten-minute prayer to the Malfeans while standing in the Labyrinth, granting total reshaping control over ten square miles of the Labyrinth for as long as Essence remains committed.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Standing within the Labyrinth, the necromancer offers a ten-minute prayer to the Malfeans and sacrifices three ghosts, destroying them, to grant herself total control over ten square miles of the Labyrinth, reshaping it to her will. While the spell is committed, she can manifest physical attacks (using Wits plus the appropriate combat Ability plus Occult successes) or create hazards and creatures at the Storyteller's discretion. Control lasts as long as the Essence remains committed, or until a dead god reclaims the reshaped space.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 140 (PDF 141), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Forsaken Life Engine
summary: Void Circle spell; conjures a yeddim-sized bone-and-iron engine that devours fed living creatures to permanently carve out a shadowland centered on itself, complete with its own combat statistics and mounted weapons.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer conjures a vast engine of bone and iron, roughly the size of a yeddim, that devours living creatures fed into it. Once creatures with a cumulative permanent Essence of at least ten times the motes spent have been consumed, the engine carves out a permanent shadowland with a fifty-mile radius (extendable by another fifty miles per additional ten motes spent) centered on itself. The engine has Strength 6, Dexterity 4, Stamina 6, Perception 2, Intelligence 2, Wits 4, a relevant combat Ability of 3, soaks of 22L/30B, and sixty health levels; damage must exceed its soak to harm it at all, Obsidian Countermagic destroys it instantly, and Adamant Countermagic deals ten health levels of damage to it. It can process up to five creatures per minute (one every four turns) and self-destructs in a fiery explosion with a five-hundred-yard blast radius if destroyed. Its weapons are Engine Claws (Speed -2, Accuracy +3, Damage +6L, Defense +0), Fragment (Accuracy +0, Damage +7L, Rate 3, Range 100), and Blood (Accuracy +3, Damage +6L, Rate 1, Range 25).
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 140 (PDF 141), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Grandmother Void
summary: Void Circle spell; the caster becomes a flat, empty silhouette — a living doorway into Oblivion — that spawns fully material spectres each turn to obey her commands in the Malfeans' name, at the risk of a taint roll for anyone who hears their whispers.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Speaking two words of the Old Realm tongue, the necromancer becomes a flat, empty silhouette — a doorway into Oblivion — for a number of turns equal to her Essence. Each turn, two spectres spawn fully formed from her, complete with full Essence and health levels, created using the starting ghost rules plus bonus experience equal to seven times the necromancer's Essence, with stats set by the necromancer herself. These spectres obey the necromancer's commands in the name of the Malfeans. Hearing their whispers risks a Willpower + Essence roll at difficulty 5 to avoid Oblivion's taint (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 284). While the caster is filled with infinite nothingness in this form, she is immune to physical and mental assaults; Obsidian or Adamant Countermagic cast during this period returns her to herself and ends the spell early, but will not dispel any spectres she has already brought forth.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 142 (PDF 143), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Mouth of the Void
summary: Void Circle mass-death spell; the caster's mouth yawns open, pouring out a spreading darkness that devours every living creature within a forty-yard radius, dealing thirty levels of aggravated damage and leaving the ground pitted with obsidian.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer intones dark words, and cold shadows flare about her mouth like the lashing tails of a hundred preying cats. As she speaks, her mouth yawns wide and darkness pours out, rippling outward like an oil slick to fill a forty-yard radius over the course of the casting. As the spell ends, the darkness stills before falling into the sky like a silent reverse waterfall, blotting out all light within its boundary as it does. To anyone caught within, the blackness feels alive, clawing, grasping, whispering, and nibbling, removing parts of their innermost flesh and being. After the shadow takes these things, it leaves them, departing for the Void and the end of all life: each living creature within its reach suffers thirty levels of aggravated damage. The earth beneath the devouring shadow is left rotting and pitted, strewn with large chunks of obsidian — the transformed remains of any creature the spell killed.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 141 (PDF 142), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Pyre-Flame Guardian
summary: Void Circle spell; the necromancer doubles in height and fuses soulsteel skin from a dozen sacrificed ghosts to become a devastating melee combatant wreathed in unquenchable green pyre flame, exploding violently when the spell ends.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: As the casting completes, a dozen random ghosts are torn, shrieking, into Oblivion, and their anguish crawls onto the necromancer's skin, fusing into soulsteel that coats her entire body while she grows to twice her normal height. The soulsteel armor grants +12L/+12B soak and ignores any attack dealing fewer than twelve dice of raw damage. Her Strength gains a bonus equal to her Essence, and a billowing sheath of pyre flame inflicts three dice of aggravated damage upon any who dare attack her barehanded vision of harrowing death; anyone attacking with weapons not forged of stone or one of the Five Magical Materials sees their weapon slowly consumed and burned away in their hands. She can also hurl balls of pyre flame as a dice action using Thrown + Dexterity, dealing three health levels of aggravated damage plus one die per extra success, unparryable without Charms; where these flames strike, they leave circles and streaks of green fire across the scenery, and any barehanded attack that connects inflicts three more levels of aggravated damage and blows green fire blossoms across the land. Victims of the guardian's pyre flame must scrape it off (two levels of lethal damage per turn spent doing so, taking three turns) or continue burning; only creatures armored in a Magical Material, in stone, or in armor made entirely of one, are immune to the flame's spread. The spell ends when the caster cancels it, when an hour has passed (per the Calendar of Setesh), or when struck by Obsidian Countermagic; however it ends, the necromancer's soulsteel skin explodes into a thousand screaming shards traced in green fire, dealing five levels of lethal and two of aggravated damage to everyone within thirty yards, avoidable only with a perfect defense. The pyre flame this spell creates behaves as ordinary pyre flame in all respects (see Exalted: The Abyssals, p. 256): sunlight in Creation extinguishes it within minutes, in shadowlands it burns out within a year unless refreshed by sunlight, and in the Underworld it is permanent. Weapon table: Pyre-Flame Ball (Accuracy +Essence, Damage +3A, Rate 5, Range 30).
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 141 (PDF 142), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Risen and Screaming
summary: Void Circle spell; sows an area with latent undeath by walking a looped boundary, so that any living creature that later dies inside the loop rises minutes afterward as a fast, screaming zombie bound to that ground.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: Focusing dark energy inward, the necromancer walks a looped path around a stretch of fertile earth in Creation; the soil beneath her feet blackens and dries as if charred and salted as she walks. Once she completes the loop there are no immediately apparent effects, but the enclosed land has been sown with lasting undeath. Triggered by the sudden rush of spirit that accompanies any death, when a living creature breathes its last breath and falls within the boundary, the ground crumbles beneath it; the creature sinks into the dirt and rises minutes later as an animate, rotting zombie. The zombies created by this spell are under the necromancer's control if she is present; otherwise they remain stationary unless a living creature becomes visible, at which point they attempt to slay it, propagating the undeath. These zombies cannot leave the circle that birthed them — they will not try, and instantly become inanimate if forced outside the boundary. They scream loudly when they spot prey and move at twice the speed of normal zombies; lacking victims, they bury themselves in the welcoming earth (noticeable only via a Perception + Awareness roll at difficulty two), remaining perfectly aware of all creatures within ten yards and able to claw free as a turn's movement. Otherwise, they are identical to the zombies described in Exalted (p. 299) and are always extras. The enclosed area returns to normal one week per point of the necromancer's Essence after the boundary was walked, though the ground itself will never bear life again.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 143 (PDF 144), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Summon Hekatonkhire
summary: Void Circle six-hour ritual requiring the death of a mortal and a ghost (or one Ghost-Blooded); summons a monstrous hekatonkhire — a reforged fragment of a dead Primordial's soul — and forces a contested soul-duel to determine whether it serves the necromancer or destroys her.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: This six-hour ritual requires the death of both a mortal and a ghost (or a single Ghost-Blooded, see the Exalted Players Guide) as part of the casting, and ends at dusk. Once complete, it calls forth one of the great and fearsome hekatonkhire — dead-god remnants formed from the souls of things that fell in flesh alongside the Primordials during the Primordial War, myriad in shape and form. The necromancer and the summoned hekatonkhire engage in a contested Willpower + Essence duel; the necromancer may spend Essence in seven-mote increments to reduce the creature's dice pool by one die per expenditure. Rolls continue each turn until either side accumulates three more successes than the other. If the necromancer wins, the hekatonkhire serves her loyally for a year and a day, or she may set it to a single indefinite task instead; if the hekatonkhire wins, it consumes the summoner's body and soul and returns to the Underworld. [NOTE: this spell summons a Storyteller-controlled monster type; a sample hekatonkhire NPC ("Loras, Death Sun") is provided on the following page but is GM-facing content and is not reproduced in this inventory. The casting and soul-duel mechanics above are player-facing and are what this row tracks.]
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 143 (PDF 144), Book of Bone and Ebony.

name: Sins of the Father
summary: Void Circle spell; curses a living victim with eternal servitude via a never-healing facial scar that passes to all their descendants, guaranteeing that when the marked person dies they become a ghost bound to obey the caster's every command.
requirements: Necromancy: Void Circle (see Necromancy Framework and Circles).
mechanics: The necromancer lays a curse of eternal servitude upon a living victim, marking her with a scar — most commonly on the face — that never heals despite any mundane or magical treatment, and which appears identically on all of the victim's descendants while she lives. The victim can be marked in person, by lightly brushing her with the caster's fingers at the climax of the casting, or remotely through an arcane link, which is destroyed in the process. The curse inflicts no other miseries while the marked creature lives, but when she dies, she automatically becomes a ghost possessing the Passion "Obey She Who Cursed Me" at a rating equal to her new Conviction, and must immediately seek out and forever obey every command of her master. Even the caster's own death does not free the cursed line: they instead become bound to the necromancer's next incarnation, although they are free to take retribution against the original caster's reincarnation, should she rise again as a ghost herself. Obsidian Countermagic can free a single cursed individual (without freeing any relatives), while Adamant Countermagic frees a victim permanently but kills her in the process. Only a Zenith Caste priest assisted by a Solar Circle sorcerer, petitioning the Unconquered Sun, can free a victim without killing her or resorting to comparably dark magic. The Celestial Exalted cannot be enslaved by this spell, though they can still be marked and pass the curse to their children. Creatures without souls, or whose souls never enter the Underworld, are entirely immune.
compatibility: Target: One living person. Requires an arcane link for the remote variant.
notes: Chapter Five: Necromancy, The Void Circle, p. 144 (PDF 145), Book of Bone and Ebony.

summary: Void Circle necromancy spell; invests an animated war machine with a portion of the Malfeans' own power, granting it a chosen channel of entropy into Creation -- a black nimbus of destruction akin to Crypt Bolt or Withering Method, a disease-spreading effect, or some other direct conduit for Oblivion.

mechanics: Animating a war machine is sometimes just the first step toward creating a truly devastating weapon. Oblivion's Avatar invests a walking war machine with a portion of the power of the Malfeans themselves, granting it the ability to carry pure entropy into Creation. This might manifest as a black nimbus of destruction akin to the Abyssal Charms Crypt Bolt or (Material) Withering Method, the ability to spread disease, or some other form of direct channeling of Oblivion into the realm of the living; the prayer-blocking ability of the artifact weapon of mephitic desolation is cited as one product of this spell. name: Sarcophagus of Restoration
summary: Artifact ••• catalog item from Creations of Bone. A black marble-and-soulsteel coffin that heals whoever sleeps within it -- ghosts, Abyssals, the living, or even reasonably intact corpses -- though living sleepers risk Willpower loss and derangement from the nightmares it inflicts.
requirements: Artifact Background (see the artifact's rating for cost).
mechanics: Carved of two heavy slabs of black marble joined with hinged soulsteel bands, this coffin's effect depends on who sleeps within it. A ghost inside falls into Slumber as though the coffin were a Fetter and heals with a bonus success on waking. An Abyssal Exalt falls into an eight-hour torpor, loses a dot of Resonance (or, if she has none, adds a success to her Willpower-regaining Conviction roll) and heals as a Slumbering ghost using Essence in place of Stamina; Ghost-Blooded and Shadewalkers get the same benefit without a Resonance cost. Other living beings fall comatose and heal like ghosts, but suffer a point of Willpower drain, forfeit their usual Conviction roll, and must beat an escalating Willpower check each night or gain a psychosis- or moral-degeneration-flavored derangement. The sarcophagus can also mend fresh or mummified corpses placed within it, healing rot as lethal damage each eight-hour cycle. It needs no extra power inside an Underworld or shadowland Manse, but requires a socketed Hearthstone (or a soulfire gem draining 3 motes per cycle) elsewhere in the lands of the dead, and a level-3+ Hearthstone or 10 motes per cycle from an attending Essence-channeler within Creation proper. Resisting its sleep requires a Stamina + Resistance roll (difficulty 3) each turn.
compatibility: Artifact Traits: not restated in the source text for this entry (large environmental/furniture-scale artifact); see mechanics for full functional rules.

As armor it grants 9L/9B soak with a -2 mobility penalty and 0 fatigue value, raises the wearer's Strength by 2 and Stamina by 1 on all rolls, completely negates fatigue and encumbrance penalties (though the wearer still cannot exceed his adjusted lift value), and negates dice penalties from pain or wounds (though injuries still apply their other effects). It is typically issued by the Mask of Winters to nemissaries or brutally trained elite mortal troops.

name: Manifestation Engine
summary: Artifact ••••+ catalog item from Creations of Bone. A nested-sphere soulsteel device that grants a ghost (or an entire war machine, for larger versions) solid substance in Creation for as long as its internal Essence-containing gem holds out, at real risk of catastrophic failure if it runs dry or is exposed to sunlight while depleted.
requirements: Artifact Background (see the artifact's rating for cost).
mechanics: A manifestation engine consists of nested spheres of rune-engraved soulsteel filigree, ranging from a fist-sized personal pendant that must touch its wearer's corpus to ten-foot versions meant to keep entire Deathlord war machines solid in Creation. While active, it keeps a ghost (or war machine) as solid in Creation as the Arcanos Weighted With the Anchor of Flesh would. Even the smallest engine houses an Artifact ••• Essence-containing gem shielded against Creation's ambient decay, with shielding soak of 5L/3B per point of the engine's own Artifact rating and two health levels of toughness per rating point before cracking; a cracked or breached engine instantly and audibly discharges its entire Essence reserve. A full engine typically holds enough Essence for 24 hours of solidity; if it runs dry at night the wearer simply fades back to the Underworld, but if it runs dry during the day it instead devours the wearer's Essence, then Willpower, then health levels (two per hour) before forcing the fade -- and if caught by direct sunlight while feeding this way, it explodes for 10 lethal health levels of damage to everyone within ten feet. The internal gem can be refilled with the Arcanos Filling the Precious Vial, or recharges itself at 1 mote per day while in the Underworld or a death-aspected Manse. Only Deathlords and extremely powerful, skilled ghosts can create new manifestation engines, which command astronomical black-market prices among ghosts with unfinished business in the living world.

name: Becoming the Wood Friend
summary: Terrestrial Circle (Circle of Emerald) spell. With a swirl of emerald mist, the caster channels Essence into herself and creates an empathic bond with the elemental aspect of wood. The caster's skin gains a greenish cast, and her hair becomes like leaves.
requirements: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery (see terrestrial-circle-sorcery).
mechanics: With a swirl of emerald mist, the caster channels Essence into herself and creates an empathic bond with the elemental aspect of wood. The caster's skin gains a greenish cast, and her hair becomes like leaves. The sorcerer can now feel the living plants and trees around her with supernatural clarity, and nature itself responds to the caster's desires. Until the next time she sleeps, the caster may move unhindered through even the densest foliage and can run at top speed in it without Athletics rolls. This spell does not protect the caster from rocks, mud or dangerous animals, but even mindless carnivorous plants will think the caster more plant than prey. Intelligent plant life feels an empathic bond with the caster of Becoming the Wood Friend but can choose to ignore the effects at will. For purposes of speed and fatigue rolls, any forest, scrubland or even cultivated field is treated as open terrain to a sorcerer under the effects of this spell. In addition, no method of mundane tracking can be used to follow the being. Even the target's scent becomes more like the plants she passes through. The sorcerer may engage in supernatural tracking contests, and supernatural trackers suffer a +2 difficulty to rolls made to track the caster. This sorcery renders useless any Charm or other effect that makes the caster harder to track. In addition, the caster becomes completely at home in the trees. She adds her Essence Trait to her Strength when determining her jumping distance when leaping or brachiating through wooded environments. She also adds her Essence Trait to her Dexterity when determining her base movement speeds in forests, jungles, savannas or other green environment. finally, she adds her Essence Trait to any other Athletic rolls involving moving through or balancing on plant life. The empathic bond works on the sorcerer as well as plants. She must make a successful Willpower roll to do any serious harm to a plant or tree. She cannot cut live wood or set unprotected fires, nor can she join in a large scale harvest. Gathering fruits or nuts, gathering fallen wood or pruning dead branches does not count as serious harm. Performing such an act of harm instantly ends the spell effect, and the caster is unable to use this spell again for three whole days under such circumstances.
notes: Chapter Five: Spells, Terrestrial Circle (Circle of Emerald), p. 101 (PDF 102), Savant and Sorcerer.

name: Blood Lash
summary: Terrestrial Circle (Circle of Emerald) spell. When this spell is cast, blood explodes from the casters wounds, and Essence twists this blood and the caster's pain into a lethal red whip. To cast blood lash, the sorcerer must have suffered at least one health level of lethal damage without healing and must pay not only the motes of Essence necessary, but an additional health level of lethal damage.
requirements: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery (see terrestrial-circle-sorcery).
mechanics: When this spell is cast, blood explodes from the casters wounds, and Essence twists this blood and the caster's pain into a lethal red whip. To cast blood lash, the sorcerer must have suffered at least one health level of lethal damage without healing and must pay not only the motes of Essence necessary, but an additional health level of lethal damage. This health level represents the blood loss necessary to form the physical aspect of the spell. Such damage is a committed cost and does not trigger reflexive Charms, nor does it heal until the spell ends. The blood lash appears as a whip of swirling vermilion liquid, anchored to the caster's wounds and wrapping around his limbs to protrude from his weapon hand. The blood lash, though a weapon, is also a part of the sorcerer's body and cannot be disarmed or taken away. The blood lash has a speed equal to the sorcerer's Occult score and an accuracy and defense of +1 each. The caster uses his Dexterity + Melee pool to attack and deals a base lethal damage of his Strength + permanent Essence + the number of health levels of lethal damage from which he is currently suffering. The sorcerer may make attacks against targets up to a range in yards equal to his Willpower Trait. For Example: Rosh the Triumphant is fighting for his life (and the lives of a small group of villagers) against a tyrant lizard. He has taken three health levels of bashing damage and four levels of lethal damage. When he casts blood lash, he takes an additional level of lethal damage, for a total of five lethal health levels. His Strength and Essence are both 3, making his damage with the sorcerous weapon equal to 11L (3 Essence + 3 Strength + 5 health levels). His Willpower is 8, allowing him to attack the creature from up to eight yards away. The caster of blood lash must concentrate while using the weapon, so no other spells may be cast until it is dispelled. Charms may be used normally.
