No splat-specific eligibility restriction; cross-referenced to this splat's own virtues-of-death row since an Abyssal's Virtue specialty condition should be framed in terms of her Virtues of Death (e.g. a loyal deathknight's Conviction specialty around "unwavering loyalty to my Deathlord," or a renegade's Valor specialty around "defying the Malfeans' will").

name: Driving Passion
summary: A Nature-tied all-consuming goal (liberating a nation, avenging a loved one's murder) that grants a bonus die whenever the character takes action directly furthering it; resolving or betraying it changes the character's Traits.
mechanics: Characters with a Driving Passion live for a cause directly tied to their Nature (most commonly Architect or Visionary). The cause can be anything of any scope, from liberating the Threshold from the tyranny of the Realm to avenging a loved one's murder to becoming a peerless master swordsman. Whenever the character takes action directly furthering this goal, his player adds one additional die to the roll involved. The Storyteller remains the final arbiter of what situations merit this bonus. A character seeking vengeance for his dead wife would certainly gain dice when searching for clues, disputing the murderer's flunkies and the final dramatic duel with the killer. However, the character would not gain a bonus in combat with roadside brigands on the way to the murderer's home city because the combat is only tangentially connected to the Driving Passion. If a character actually resolves or fulfills her Driving Passion, she immediately loses this Merit and gains six experience points.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- a deathknight could easily hold a Driving Passion tied to her service to (or rebellion against) her Deathlord.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-driving-passion): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged. Thematically fits either a loyal deathknight's driving cause (perfecting her Deathlord's mandate) or a renegade's (finding redemption, protecting the living she left behind).

name: Tactical Instincts
summary: Intuitive grasp of tactics: with a Wits + Lore roll, instantly discerns weaknesses/distribution of forces in a battle or game board, building a bonus pool usable to aid Wits/Presence rolls to command forces.
mechanics: The character has an intuitive understanding of tactics, from the myriad stratagems of Gateway to the most elaborate battlefield formations. With a Wits + Lore roll at standard difficulty, the character, upon glancing at any contested forces or the arrangement of a game board, immediately discerns all weaknesses and distribution of strength. Successes accumulate as a pool of extra dice the character's player may subsequently apply to any Lore rolls to devise a winning strategy or Presence rolls to command forces in pursuit of that victory. Other pertinent rolls may benefit from this pool with Storyteller permission. No more than three of these dice may be applied to any single roll, and bonus dice remain unused until the end of the scene. Characters may not reevaluate the tactical scenario to refresh their bonus pool until they use it again.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted, including deathknights who command Abyssal Command troops or the armies of the dead.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-tactical-instincts): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; cross-referenced to this splat's own Abyssal Command Background since this Merit's Presence-based bonus for commanding forces pairs naturally with that Background for a deathknight general.

name: True Love
summary: A deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates; adds one die to rolls in defense of or aid of that loved one, and if the lover perishes the character may substitute this bond for Conviction to regain Willpower. For an Abyssal, taking a willing lover from among the living is itself a Litany of Sins trigger (1 point of Resonance per night of intimacy).
mechanics: A character with this Merit shares a deep and abiding romance with a partner who reciprocates that affection. This commitment adds one die to all rolls in defense or aid of that loved one. As always, the Storyteller remains the final authority of what actions receive this bonus. The player of a character with this Merit may also roll (Compassion + 1) in place of Conviction for her character to regain Willpower each morning, if so desired. If the character's lover perished, she immediately loses this Merit, but she may subsume her feelings into an appropriate Driving Passion, with Storyteller approval. Such passions often focus on completing the work of the deceased, honoring her memory or avenging her untimely demise.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted, though a deathknight's True Love is thematically loaded: if the beloved is living, the relationship itself steadily accrues Resonance per this splat's own gaining-resonance rule (1 point per night of intimacy with a living lover), making True Love as much a liability as a comfort for a loyal servant of the Deathlords.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-true-love): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: cross-referenced to gaining-resonance, since "taking a willing lover from among the living" is a named Litany of Sins trigger (1 Resonance/night of intimacy) -- a deathknight with True Love for a living partner is mechanically choosing ongoing Resonance risk for the sake of that bond, a strong story hook this splat's own Resonance system already supports.

name: True Paragon
summary: The character exudes formal-code honor and nobility; may spend bonus points/experience to raise Virtues above the normal 5 maximum (up to 6), and may roll her highest Virtue in place of Conviction to regain Willpower while asleep. Restricted to characters with the Paragon Nature.
mechanics: The character exudes honor and nobility, either from a formal code or an instinctive fulfillment of what she believes is right. As a result, she may spend bonus and experience points to raise any Virtue to a rating of 6. Characters with this Merit capable of raising their Virtues above 5 for other reasons instead add one to their permitted maximum. This Merit does not allow permanent Willpower to exceed a rating of 10. In addition, the player of a character with this Merit may choose to roll her character's highest Virtue in place of the standard Conviction roll for her character to regain Willpower after sleeping. Only characters with the Paragon Nature may purchase or retain this Merit. Characters who betray their code lose this Merit without compensation.
compatibility: Any character type with the Paragon Nature; no splat-specific variant is given. An Abyssal with the Paragon Nature -- whether a Deathlord-devoted zealot who has made an unbending code of her service, or a renegade devoted to an equally rigid code of redemption -- qualifies normally.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-true-paragon): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Restriction is by Nature (Paragon), not by Exalt type, so it transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Jack of All Trades
summary: Broad basis of knowledge and skill, with an almost preternatural ability to adapt understanding to new purposes; suffers no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit have a broad basis of knowledge and skill to draw upon and an almost preternatural ability to adapt their understanding to new purposes and situations. They suffer no penalty to Attribute rolls lacking the required Ability for a dice pool.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-jack-of-all-trades): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Born to Rule
summary: Conveys authority in every gesture and inflection; adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit convey authority in every gesture and inflection, most likely as a result of aristocratic upbringing. Others develop such majesty through the practice of leadership or upon receiving the mantle of Exaltation. Regardless, this Merit adds one die to all Social rolls when interacting with an acknowledged inferior (as determined by the Storyteller).
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fits Abyssal deathknights particularly well, given their standing as generals, princes and terrible lords within their Deathlords’ courts.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-born-to-rule): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Enchanting Feature
summary: A striking, attractive feature or strong presence the character can exploit to add one die to pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller.
mechanics: Something about the character is striking and attractive or at least conveys a strong presence. He may have deep eyes that seem to hold the secrets of the universe or a voice that resonates like the basso rumble of a lion. Whenever the character can exploit this feature, he adds one die to all pertinent Social rolls, as decided by the Storyteller.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Available to Abyssal Exalted, particularly those whose undeath has not yet visibly marked them -- a still-beautiful deathknight can weaponize that unchanged beauty precisely because it hides what she has become.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-enchanting-feature): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged. Pairs thematically with the Disfigured Flaw at the opposite end of the spectrum -- a deathknight who resists visible decay may keep this Merit instead of taking on a rotted visage.

name: Innocuous
summary: The two-point version makes the character forgettable and hard to pick out of a crowd; the four-point (Supernatural) version cloaks the character's identity from memory almost entirely.
mechanics: Characters with the two-point version of this Merit have an eerily unremarkable visage. Height, weight and build are all average, all plain. No one is apt to pick them from a crowd unless their skin and hair is dramatically different in hue than all the locals -- and, possibly, not even then. People are less likely to remember them at all if they do nothing to draw attention to themselves. Such everyman anonymity adds one die to pertinent Larceny and Stealth rolls and adds one to the difficulty of any casual pursuit or investigation of the character. This will not foil any serious inquiry, nor does it grant any bonus if the character is alone or does something memorable (such as showing any level of an anima banner). Characters must have Appearance 2 in order to purchase this version of Innocuous. The four-point version of Innocuous is a Supernatural Merit rather than Social. The character is not simply ordinary, but is cloaked in an aura of subtle obscurity. Those who witness and even interact with her find their memories blurred. They may recall the conversation, but not the person with whom they spoke. Mechanically, this more powerful version doubles the bonuses afforded by the lesser version of this Merit. Additionally, onlookers do not remember more than superficial details from interactions with the character without a Wits + Essence roll. The base difficulty of this roll is 6, reduced by 1 for every significant event that occurred with the character in the previous week. Once a witness pierces the anonymity, the difficulty of subsequent memory checks is the number of full weeks she has gone without interacting with the obscured character. This roll is made once a week, starting with the first full week of no contact. On a failure, existing memories of previous encounters with the obscured character blur and fade regardless of their significance. Magical beings (those with Essence 2+) indefinitely ignore the aura of anonymity after they pierce it once, but only if the hidden character has a lower permanent Essence. Unfortunately, magically cloaked characters have obvious difficulties forming relationships and may not have more than two Contacts, Mentor or any other socially dependent Backgrounds unless their associates are powerful magical beings assumed to have pierced the veil. Veiled characters may not have Followers, Henchman, a Cult, any form of Command or other Backgrounds contingent on being widely known without extremely unusual circumstances approved by the Storyteller. Sidereals may not purchase Innocuous in either version, as their innate Arcane Fate supersedes the Merit's effects. The effects of Innocuous do not stack with Charms and other magic that conceal identity. Only the most powerful effect applies.
compatibility: EXCLUDED for Sidereal Exalted only ("Sidereals may not purchase Innocuous in either version, as their innate Arcane Fate supersedes the Merit's effects"). No restriction is stated against Abyssals; fully available at both tiers (2-pt. version requires Appearance 2+). Note that Abyssal characters with the four-point version and the Followers/Liege/Whispers/Cult Backgrounds should reconcile the Merit's socially-dependent-Background cap with the Liege Background all deathknights innately possess -- Storyteller's call on how visibly a cloaked deathknight can still serve as her Deathlord's agent.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-innocuous): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. This Merit explicitly excludes only Sidereal Exalted; no restriction applies to Abyssals, so it is selectable at both tiers for this splat.

name: Favor
summary: As a Merit, someone of roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor, scaled 1-4 points by the severity/danger of the service that would repay it (2/4/6 points for minor/moderate/major favors owed by Yu-Shan's Celestial courts); as a Flaw, the character owes such a favor to someone else.
mechanics: If this Trait is a Merit, someone roughly equal or greater power owes the character a favor. The value of this Merit depends on the extent of service required to cancel the debt. For one point, the debtor must perform a task that might take a few days but would not place her in any foreseen danger or require her to go especially out of her way. For two points, the debtor must perform a service whose execution may involve considerable inconvenience but little danger. Three-point favors are quite serious, and may involve substantial risk of injury or other misfortune. Four-point favors can be repaid by directly saving the favor holder's life or fulfilling any single task she demands whenever she demands it. In the convoluted politics of Yu-Shan and the great spirit courts, a minor Celestial favor is worth two points, a moderate favor worth four points and a major favor costs six points. This Trait may also be taken as a Flaw, in which case the character owes a favor to someone powerful enough and well-connected enough to call it in. The value of this Trait depends on the severity of favor as noted previously. Characters with Backing or similar Backgrounds most likely owe this to another member of their organization or at least to a well-regarded associate. For other characters, the possibilities are limitless: Guild factors, politicians, merciful victors of a duel, etc. Characters who renege on their favors will suffer considerable loss of face at best and possibly much worse if they break their word to someone powerful or vengeful. In either form as a Merit or a Flaw, a Favor lasts until the holder calls it due. Once paid, the Trait becomes null, without adding or subtracting experience or other recompense. Storytellers should not go easy on characters who owe favors, even at low levels. Indebtedness is not pleasant or convenient, and a mundane errand called due in the middle of an epic quest can create all sorts of life complications. It is common practice among spirit courts and in certain groups to exchange their favors as social currency. In such systems, a favor debt may be transferred to another party in order to cancel a debt of like value. Such transfers do not need the consent of the party who owes the service. This practice can lead to considerable complications if a god purchases a favor from characters who haven't even heard of it, especially if that god has a diametrically opposed agenda to those owing it in service.
compatibility: Any character type; the higher-value tiers (2/4/6 points) specifically describe favors owed within Yu-Shan's Celestial spirit courts, but nothing restricts this Trait away from any Exalted type, including Abyssals -- a deathknight is just as likely to hold (or owe) a favor from a Deathlord's court, a powerful ghost, or an Underworld spirit as from Yu-Shan.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-flaw-favor): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; the 2/4/6-point Celestial-favor tier is a Yu-Shan setting detail, but an Abyssal could equally hold or owe an equivalent-value favor from a power within the Underworld's own hierarchy (a Deathlord, a powerful ghost court, or a Malfean-adjacent spirit).

name: Heirloom
summary: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than her means and lifestyle can afford, for only one bonus point regardless of the item’s Resource value.
mechanics: The character owns a piece of property more valuable than his means and lifestyle can afford. Such treasures may be actual heirlooms, spoils of a heist, gifts or something more exotic still. Such an item costs only one bonus point regardless of its Resource value. Most weapons and armor purchased with Heirloom will be of exceptional quality. This Merit is particularly easy to abuse and sufficient value to raise a character's Resources rating if sold; the Storyteller should probably require purchase of Resources at that level and assume that the wealth is simply concentrated into very narrow holdings.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-heirloom): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Hidden Manse
summary: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history/geomantic maps, or one shrouded by a mysterious property of its arcane nature; requires the Manse Background.
mechanics: The character controls a Manse forgotten to history and geomantic maps or perhaps a Manse in a more public area shrouded by some mysterious property of its arcane nature. Such a hidden place of power makes an excellent base of operations or secret lair, provided that the character and those trusted with the secret don't compromise the location with their actions. Assuming the character is properly discrete, no one need ever know about his magical lair. This Merit costs one point for a hidden Demesne or two points for an actual Manse. Characters must have the Manse Background to purchase this Merit.
compatibility: Any character type with the Manse Background; no splat-specific variant is given. For Abyssal Exalted, this Merit attaches to whichever of this splat's two Manse-equivalent Backgrounds the hidden site belongs to: the altered Manse Background (for a site in the land of the living, purchased normally per manse-background-altered) or the Underworld Manse Background (for a site within the Underworld itself, per underworld-manse-background) -- an especially fitting use, since the Deathlords already claim few Manses of either kind and a hidden one is a genuine prize.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-hidden-manse): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: this splat has two Manse-equivalent Backgrounds instead of one core-Exalted Manse Background (manse-background-altered for the living world, underworld-manse-background for the Underworld), so this row cross-references both; either can host a Hidden Manse.

name: Heir Apparent
summary: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by their parents or another benefactor once the current owner dies (or is otherwise removed); each point invested grants two dots of Backgrounds ultimately gained, cumulative with existing Backgrounds.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit will receive an inheritance left by their parents or another benefactor. They only need to wait for the current owner to die -- or find some way to hasten that process along without getting caught (which would forfeit the gain at the very least). Every point invested in this Merit grants two dots of Backgrounds that the character will ultimately gain, but no single Background may gain more than five points in this fashion. The Storyteller may add a die to a stipulated inheritance's difficulty for every major condition attached to it. This can require that the character be married or unmarried, serve in the military for a defined number of years, etc. Background dots obtained with this Merit are cumulative with Backgrounds the character already possesses and may raise a Background above a rating of four. Although Heir Apparent is typically used to transfer resources, artifacts, followers and other tangible goods or benefits, it may also include business partners or associates in the form of contacts, allies and the like. More exotic selections rely on situation and Storyteller approval, such as a necromancer whose blood-inscribed heir will bestow her Whispers to her heir.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- a deathknight could inherit dots of Resources, Artifact, Followers or another eligible Background from a mortal benefactor, a deceased predecessor deathknight, or even (at Storyteller discretion) an increase to her standing with her Deathlord.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-heir-apparent): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged. The source text's own necromancer example ("a necromancer whose blood-inscribed heir will bestow her Whispers to her heir") is a near-literal fit for this splat's own Whispers Background.

name: Legendary Artifact
summary: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power (on par with the Mantle of Brigid or the Eye of Autochthon); the book explicitly discourages Storytellers from ever allowing it, calling such artifacts "innately and grossly unfair plot devices."
mechanics: A character with this Merit has gotten hold of an artifact of world-shaking power, a relic on par with the Mantle of Brigid or the Eye of Autochthon. These rare and often unwisely coveted devices invariably reshape the lives of all who come into contact with them, defining even the epoch of their use. These relics bring terrible danger commensurate with their power, as the doomed prophet Ikere and Bagrash Kol learned in their futile attempts to master the fabled Eye. And then too, these devices attract the worst and deadliest ambitions of gods and demons and Exalted hungry for their power. Storytellers do not need to allow this Merit ever, as legendary artifacts are innately and grossly unfair plot devices that will likely dominate any series they occupy. This Trait merely aids in telling stories revolving around these relics.
compatibility: Any character type, at Storyteller discretion (heavily discouraged by the book's own text); no splat-specific variant is given. Available to Abyssal Exalted at the same heavy discretion as any other splat.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-legendary-artifact): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Cache
summary: The character has wealth hidden or legally stored across many locations, for one bonus point per city beyond the character’s home; requires Resources 4+ or Salary 2+.
mechanics: The character has wealth hidden or legally stored in banks in many locations, for a cost of one bonus point per city beyond the character's home. The character has full access to the value of his full Resources or Salary at any of these locations and their surrounding regions. Characters with five points of Cache are assumed to have access to their wealth in any settlement town-sized or larger in a selected direction of Creation or the Blessed Isle, though it may take up to a week for the money to arrive within that domain by another direction. Every additional point beyond five extends this domain by another direction. Characters must have Resources 4+ or Salary 2+ to purchase this Merit.
compatibility: Any character type with Resources 4+ or Salary 2+; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted using the standard, unaltered Resources Background (the Liege Background can grant bonus points toward Resources, per this splat’s own liege-background row, but does not change how Cache itself works).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-cache): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged, using the standard core-Exalted Resources/Salary Backgrounds (not altered for this splat).

name: Alternative Divination
summary: Crude divination through methods other than astrology (tea leaves, entrails, palm-reading, crystal-gazing, etc.); each purchase grants knowledge of one ritual, capped by the character's Occult rating.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit can crudely divine the workings of fate through methods other than astrology. Some read destiny in the pattern of tea leaves or the entrails of birds or upon the symbolic verses of a spider's web, while others spout disjointed verses of prophecy from a drug-induced trance or read palms or gaze into crystals. Whatever the method, the rolls and effectiveness of divination remain the same as for conventional astrology (see Exalted, p. 251). Any divination ritual should take a minimum of one scene to complete, though most will be considerably longer. Methods less complicated and quicker than astrology suffer an increased difficulty assigned by the Storyteller, while complicated, well-described rituals should benefit from a stunt bonus. Characters may purchase this Merit multiple times, with each purchase granting knowledge of one effective ritual by astrology (or two rituals per purchase for Sidereal Exalted). However, characters may not purchase this Merit more times than their Occult rating.
compatibility: Any character type with an Occult rating; Sidereal Exalted specifically get two rituals learned per purchase instead of one, which does not extend to Abyssal Exalted. Thematically strong fit for Abyssal characters -- a deathknight's divination method could as easily be reading entrails or bones as tea leaves, dovetailing with this splat's own death-magic Occult specialties.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-alternative-divination): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The Sidereal-specific two-ritual bonus is retained in this row's compatibility text for reference but does not apply to Abyssal, who purchase this Merit at the standard one-ritual-per-purchase rate.

name: Priest
summary: Recognized priest of a deity/religion; the 1-pt. version is automatically and freely granted to Zenith, MIDNIGHT (Abyssal), and No Moon Caste Exalted (and to all Sidereal Exalted for their initiating astrological college) as an innate part of their Exaltation. The 7-pt. high-priest version costs those same castes only 6 points, but their Caste Mark glows during miracle prayers.
mechanics: The character is a recognized priest of a particular deity or religion. Apart from lowering the difficulty of prayers directed at the appropriate spirit (see Exalted, p. 335), the one-point version of this Merit has no defined rules effects. Storytellers may award symbolic dream messages to priests or promise dream omens sent by their patron, but no systems govern these visitations. The effects of this Merit are automatically bestowed upon Zenith, Midnight and No Moon Caste Exalted, and all Sidereal Exalted are automatically priests of the astrological colleges they are initiated into. Such characters do not need to purchase this Merit, as it is an innate aspect of their Exaltation. The seven-point version of this Merit signifies far greater favor from the priest's spirit patron. Such high priests receive portentous dreams and even waking visions from their masters, but their devotion and faith must be ever-unwavering to retain favor. Piety has its rewards, however, and high priests may petition the god, elemental or demon they serve for miracles. A petition of this magnitude is performed as a standard prayer roll, though the player must spend a Willpower point to make an automatic success or channel a Virtue appropriate to the prayer. Provided that god, elemental or demon accepts the petition (Storyteller's discretion), successes on this attempt may be spent to: restore one point to the character's Essence pool (one success), restore one spent Willpower point to the character's pool (two successes), exorcise a possessing spirit from a host (requires successes equal to the offending spirit's Essence + 3, and the character's patron must have a higher Essence rating than the targeted spirit) or heal a dying character to stable condition at Incapacitated (five successes; Resources 4+ offering required). Storytellers may allow other specialized prayers at their discretion, using the preceding list as inspiration for the level of power and number of successes required for miracles. It is also important to remember that some spirits will not or cannot perform certain miracles based on their nature or power. Spirits can perceive a distinctive mark upon characters with this Merit. The design and placement of this mark depends on the patron. Exalted castes who are innate priests of their gods pay only six points to become high priests, but their Caste Mark glows brightly whenever they pray for a miracle.
cost: 1- or 7-pt. Merit, 6-pt. high priest for Midnight Caste
compatibility: Midnight Caste Abyssals get the 1-pt. version automatically and for free as an innate part of their Exaltation (no purchase needed), and pay only 6 points (not 7) for the high-priest upgrade -- with their Caste Mark glowing brightly during miracle prayers. Dusk, Daybreak, Day, and Moonshadow Caste Abyssals purchase this Merit normally at full cost like any other Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-priest): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. EXPLICIT ABYSSAL CASTE MENTION carried over verbatim from the source: the mechanics text names "Zenith, Midnight and No Moon Caste Exalted" as the three castes who are innate priests of their patron -- Midnight Caste is one of the five Abyssal Castes (per this splat's own midnight-caste row), so this Merit's free 1-pt. grant and discounted 6-pt. high-priest upgrade apply directly to Midnight Caste deathknights. This is a splat-specific benefit that transfers essentially unchanged from the Players Guide's own text, not something derived by analogy from Lunar's row.

name: Destiny
summary: Represents an auspicious fate written in the stars, scaling from a lifetime of good health (1 pt.) up to founding a lasting noble dynasty or transforming an era (5 pts.); a companion sidebar states Celestial Exalted (Solar, Lunar, Sidereal) AND ABYSSAL/INFERNAL EXALTED may only retain 1-2 points of Destiny after Exaltation consumes the rest, while Terrestrial (Dragon-Blooded) and Alchemical Exalted have no such cap.
mechanics: A character with Destiny shall live most auspiciously, his fate written large in the stars above. Providence comes in many forms and degrees of fortune, as represented by the number of points invested in this Merit. A one-point destiny may be a long and uneventful life of good health without serious hunger. Two points promise a lifetime of financial prosperity or many offspring to carry the family name -- or perhaps the greater prosperity of a famed tradesman, local hero or honored elder. In three points lie the destinies of merchant princes, kings of small nations and those of similar ilk. The favored scion of a Dynastic house might bear such a fate, as might the conscript who survives and rises through the ranks to become a general in his own right. Four points promise the life of a hero whose deeds shall live on in songs and stories for many generations to come or perhaps the founder of a lasting noble dynasty. Five-point destinies only surround the mightiest sorcerers and emperors whose exploits transform their era and world. The combined fate of entire nations bends before such epochal figures. While ultimately positive in its way, destiny need not be kind to those who bear it or those who stand in its path. A foreordained king may claim his crown through assassination and treachery, his greatness rooted in tyranny. Conversely, a selfless hero may deliver her people from that same tyrant through her martyrdom, her greatness culminating in personal tragedy even as her name becomes legend. Such juxtapositions of greatness and doom may best be represented by a combination of this Merit and the Dark Fate Flaw (see p. 39). Characters bearing the twin marks of fortune and misfortune will fulfill both in their own way, usually through the same events as those bearing Destiny with a single success. Any astrologer can sense the weight of fortune upon the horoscope of those bearing this Merit, though discerning the specifics of such a destiny requires far more effort and research. It is worth noting the difference between capacity for greatness and certainty of greatness. All Exalted bear the capacity to become mighty heroes or despots by virtue of their power, yet not all do so by virtue of the very free will granted by that potential. Those with Destiny must fulfill that fate unless the power of the Maidens, and even the Celestials, can alter the fate of the dead and Abyssal Exalted. It is incumbent upon Storytellers to ensure that coincidence protects those with a powerful fate until that fate finds fruition, though such protection may seem cruel or callous. Such characters are not wholly defended from misfortune and injury, but only such misfortune as directly interferes with their appointed role. There is no mystery or system for such protection, as it is no more a storytelling matter. Players who invest points in this Merit may request a particular destiny for their characters or leave the specifics in the hands of the Storyteller. As always, Storytellers should feel free to veto any destiny that they find inappropriate for their story. A companion sidebar, 'Destiny and Exaltation,' explains that Terrestrial Exaltation flows through bloodline and luck, but Celestial Exaltation (Solar, Lunar, Sidereal) only affixes itself to mortals of sufficient Destiny -- Destiny 3 or better for Solars and Lunars, Destiny 4 or better for Sidereals -- and Abyssal/Infernal Exaltation likewise requires Destiny 3. When Celestial Exaltation takes place, the new Exalt's free will overrides most of that predetermined fate, reducing the character's Destiny rating by four (for Sidereals) or three (for the rest) and folding the remainder into minor fates; as a result, Celestial, Abyssal and Infernal Exalted can only retain the smallest of destinies and may not purchase or hold more than one or two points of this Merit after Exaltation. Terrestrial (Dragon-Blooded) and Alchemical Exalted do not base their Exaltations on Destiny and, therefore, suffer no such cap.
cost: 1- to 5-pt. Merit, 1- to 2-pt. cap for Abyssal Exalted
compatibility: Available to mortals at full 1-5 pt. range. Abyssal (and Infernal) Exalted are explicitly capped at 1-2 points of Destiny after Exaltation, per the companion sidebar, and per that same sidebar a mortal needed Destiny 3+ before Exaltation to be a viable candidate for the Deathlords' dark gift in the first place.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-destiny): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. EXPLICIT ABYSSAL MENTION carried over verbatim from the source's 'Destiny and Exaltation' sidebar: it groups "Abyssal/Infernal Exaltation" with Celestial Exaltation as requiring Destiny 3 pre-Exaltation and then states these Exalted types "can only have the smallest of destinies" post-Exaltation, capped at 1-2 points -- unlike the Terrestrial-Bloodline and Past-Lives Merits (excluded from this pass because they name only "Celestial Exalted" without extending to Abyssal), this Merit's sidebar explicitly names Abyssal Exaltation by name, so it transfers directly with the stated 1-2-point cap. Cross-references the Dark Fate Flaw as a common thematic pairing (a deathknight with both retains fortune and doom simultaneously).

name: Lucky
summary: Grants a luck pool the player may spend to reroll dice or shift random events.
mechanics: A character with this Merit lives in interesting times, blessed with an unlikely preponderance of fortune that follows his every enterprise. He may or may not also have Destiny (see p. 25), as luck is quite a different force than fate. Those with Destiny find their luck invisibly guiding them toward that ordained end, while those without particular fate drift aimlessly and gracefully as a wind-blown leaf through the challenges of life. Lucky characters receive a luck pool equal to the number of points invested in the Merit. Players may spend points of luck to repeat any roll at the same difficulty and target number. Even botches may be rerolled with luck, provided the botches are not the result of chance guiding the character enforced by the anima of an Eclipse Caste Solar or a Moonshadow Caste Abyssal or similarly potent curses. Multiple rerolls may be applied to a single task until the desired result is obtained or until the luck runs out. Players may also spend points of luck to affect a game of chance or other completely random event involving the character. Each point spent in this manner increases the character's chance of success by 10 percent. In such situations, the Storyteller should roll one die, adding one to the result per luck point spent. If the modified result comes up 6 or higher, the event favors the character. Characters with this Merit regain one luck point after every full week they do not call upon their luck and refresh their luck pool fully at the end of each story.
compatibility: Any character type; Sidereal Exalted specifically use a different luck-pool formula (points invested + 2, capped at 5, minimum pool of 3) and pay a maximum of 3 points instead of 5, which does not extend to Abyssal Exalted. The mechanics text names "a Moonshadow Caste Abyssal" directly -- Moonshadow is one of the five Abyssal Castes -- as an example of a curse-source whose forced botches this Merit cannot reroll.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-lucky): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The mechanics text's explicit mention of "a Moonshadow Caste Abyssal" was retained verbatim since it directly names an Abyssal Caste (documenting a limitation this splat's own curse-manifestation effects can impose on OTHER Lucky characters trying to reroll around them, and equally on a Moonshadow deathknight's own botches). The Sidereal-specific luck-pool formula does not extend to Abyssal Exalted, who use the standard 1-5 pt. formula.

name: Signature Style
summary: Combines movement and attitude into a distinctive flair defining the character's legend; functions like an Ability specialty for stunts, granting an extra die that stacks with the stunt-rating die. May be purchased up to three times but only one Signature Style can benefit the same stunt.
mechanics: Characters with this Merit combine movement and attitude into a distinctive flair that defines their legend. Signature Style functions like an Ability specialty for stunts, providing one extra die in appropriate circumstances. This extra die stacks with the rating of the stunt to determine the final bonus, but it does not alter the number of motes or Willpower returned if the action succeeds. Possible Signature Style specialties include "Obvious Impossibilities," "Damn, I'm Smooth," "Making it Look Easy," "Look Upon Me and Despair," "Economy of Motion," "Excessively Flashy," "Visual Poetry" and "Shocking Brutality." As always, the Storyteller retains final authority on whether a particular action embodies the character's Signature Style. Characters may purchase this Merit up to three times, but only one Signature Style can benefit the same stunt.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- fitting examples include "Elegant Corpse-Grace," "Whispering Shroud" or "Undeniable Menace" for a deathknight’s own Signature Style.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-signature-style): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Sworn Brotherhood
summary: Exalted who took part in the Terrestrial spell Sworn Brothers’ Oath share a bond rating equal to the number of members (max 8); most commonly used to link player characters in shared purpose and loyalty (all members must buy it).
mechanics: Exalted with this Merit have taken part in the Terrestrial spell Sworn Brothers' Oath (see E:DB, p. 161), sharing a bond with a rating equal to the number of members (maximum eight). Sworn Brotherhood is most commonly used to link the players' characters together in common purpose and loyalty, and therefore, all members of the brotherhood must purchase this Merit. Sworn Brotherhood is extremely rare among Exalted other than Dragon-Blooded, though some Lunar packs bind themselves together in this fashion.
compatibility: Exalted only (not mortals). Extremely rare outside Dragon-Blooded, per the source text, but nothing bars an Abyssal from taking part in the ritual: this splat's own terrestrial-circle-sorcery row confirms deathknights can learn and cast Terrestrial Circle Sorcery, so a Circle of Abyssals (or a deathknight bonded to Dragon-Blooded allies) could plausibly cast Sworn Brothers' Oath and share this Merit.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-sworn-brotherhood): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The source text's "some Lunar packs bind themselves together in this fashion" flavor note was retained as informational, cross-splat color; it does not restrict Abyssal eligibility. This is an "Exalted only" Merit tied to a Terrestrial Circle Sorcery spell, and Abyssal Exalted have confirmed Terrestrial Circle Sorcery access per this family's own inventory, so the Merit transfers cleanly.

name: Taint's Warning
summary: A Solar Exalt with this Merit intuitively senses demons, Infernal Exalted, deathknights, Deathlords, the undead and other creatures of darkness within a number of yards equal to permanent Essence, lighting the Solar's Caste Mark reflexively. THE ABYSSAL VERSION instead warns the Abyssal of her OWN taint in the presence of Solar Exalted, celestial lions, mice of the sun, and other agents of the Unconquered Sun -- her Caste Mark emerges and bleeds instead of lighting up.
mechanics: A Solar Exalt with this Merit intuitively senses the presence of demons, Infernal Exalted, deathknights, Deathlords, the undead and other creatures of darkness. Whenever such a being approaches within a number of yards equal to her permanent Essence, he senses the presence and spends a mote to light his Caste Mark. This expenditure is reflexive and automatic. The Solar cannot suppress the light, although he need not expend Essence if his anima already exceeds the 4-7 range of display. The character only knows that something unclean approaches. The vague impression does not reveal the character's exact location or identity. An Abyssal with this Merit does not receive a warning of taint, but rather from her own taint. Her Caste Mark emerges and bleeds in the presence of Solar Exalted, celestial lions (see GoD, p. 33, or E:S, p. 20), mice of the sun (see CotW, pp. 15-16) and other direct agents of the Unconquered Sun.
compatibility: RESTRICTED by the Merit's own header to Solars (2-pt.) and Abyssals (1-pt.) only -- no version exists for Lunar, Sidereal, Alchemical, or Fair Folk characters. This is one of the Players Guide's rare Abyssal-exclusive (well, Abyssal-and-Solar) Merits: a deathknight with this Merit senses her own lingering taint whenever an agent of the Unconquered Sun draws near, an early-warning system against Wyld Hunt patrols, celestial lions, and mice of the sun.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-taints-warning): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. PRIMARY ABYSSAL ROW: this Merit's own header explicitly restricts it to Solars and Abyssals only, at different costs and with an inverted mechanic for each. Lunar's transcription correctly flagged this as excluded for Lunar but directly relevant for the Abyssal follow-up pass -- this is that pass. Abyssal version costs 1 point and manifests as the deathknight's own Caste Mark emerging/bleeding (rather than lighting up) whenever a Solar Exalt, celestial lion (see GoD p. 33/E:S p. 20), mouse of the sun (see CotW pp. 15-16), or similar agent of the Unconquered Sun draws near -- a warning about her own vulnerability rather than a hunter's early-warning system.

name: Prescient Dreamer
summary: Regular prophetic dreams of possible futures, deciphered with Intelligence + Occult; for a deathknight, these visions may bleed up from the Underworld or the whispers of the Malfeans as readily as from any divine patron.
mechanics: A character with this Merit regularly dreams of what may be. The reason for this may be a gift of a god capable of seeing into the future, an unconscious awareness of fate's strands, or -- for a deathknight -- an echo of the Malfeans' own dread foresight bleeding up through her Resonance-tainted Essence. Regardless of the reason, such characters always dream premonitions differently than others and recognize them as visions, even if they do not know what they mean. The futures they see may involve events of decades hence or those of the next day, though they are usually within the dreamer's lifespan. Deriving meaning from the vague symbolism of such omens requires an Intelligence + Occult roll at a significance assigned by the Storyteller to reflect the overall significance of the event. The number of successes determines the clarity of understanding. One success reveals that a great calamity will come soon, but the nature of the calamity remains disguised, as do its location and exact timing. Five successes may unearth a plot of assassination with a timetable and visions of the conspirators. Characters with this Merit do not control their visions in any way. Such dreams come unbidden and follow the whims of fate and the Storyteller. Once a character reveals memories to others or takes actions based on the dream, he interferes with that destiny and decreases its overall probability.
compatibility: Any character type; Sidereal Exalted specifically pay a reduced 2-pt. cost, which does not extend to Abyssal Exalted (they pay the standard 3-pt. cost). Thematically apt for a deathknight, whose dreams could equally be read as the Malfeans' whispers bleeding through rather than a divine gift -- this splat's own Whispers Background already documents a similar (if more targeted) form of dark cosmic insight.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-prescient-dreamer): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: this row's mechanics text was lightly adapted to add "an echo of the Malfeans' own dread foresight bleeding up through her Resonance-tainted Essence" as an in-fiction source of the visions available to a deathknight, alongside the original divine-gift/fate-awareness framing, and cross-referenced to the Whispers Background as a thematically adjacent (though mechanically distinct) form of dark insight this splat already has.

name: Eternal Vow
summary: A First-Age marriage bond blessed by Luna and the Unconquered Sun, joining Solar and Lunar Exalted (and their reincarnations) across death itself. THIS MERIT/FLAW IS EXPLICITLY RESTRICTED TO SOLARS, LUNARS AND ABYSSALS ONLY: an Abyssal who was formerly a Solar spouse from a previous incarnation typically treats the bond as a 1-point Flaw (a liability, usually paired with an Enemy rating for the aggrieved Lunar spouse), but a renegade deathknight pursuing redemption -- especially to be with her Lunar love -- may instead purchase it as the standard 3-point Merit.
mechanics: In the First Age, Solar and Lunar Exalted joined in marriages blessed by Luna and the Unconquered Sun. So strong were these vows that many endured beyond death, joining each new incarnation of Solar and Lunar Essence in matrimony. Characters with this Merit retain one of these ancient links to another Exalt. As such, they may sense the other's emotions or health across any separation of distance with a successful Perception + Essence roll. This intuition normally requires a dice action, though it may be triggered reflexively when one of the partners experiences intense feelings. It is also possible to gauge the partner's approximate direction with the intuition roll, but this requires total concentration for a full turn and cannot function unless both partners are in the same world (Creation, Yu-Shan or the Underworld). As a final benefit, the characters may reflexively donate motes to one another with a touch at the maximum rate of their Essence rating each turn. If either party dies, the survivor experiences a moment of overwhelming pain and grief and loses a number of points of temporary Willpower equal to her Compassion. If the survivor actually slew her spouse, this costs her a dot of permanent Willpower instead. Some Abyssal Exalted retain vows made in previous incarnations as Solars, much to the chagrin and enmity of surviving Lunar spouses. Deathknights linked to Lunars and vice versa treat Eternal Vow as a one-point Flaw, typically coupled with an appropriate rating of the Enemy Flaw (see p. 37). The effects of the vow remain the same, as the representation of a liability rather than an asset. Renegade deathknights pursuing the elusive hope for redemption -- especially to be with their Lunar love -- may purchase this Trait as a Merit like Solar Exalted.
compatibility: Restricted by its own header to Solars, Lunars, and Abyssals only. For an Abyssal, the typical case is the vow surviving from a previous incarnation as a Solar spouse of a Lunar -- treated as a 1-point Flaw (usually paired with the Enemy/Rival Flaw for the surviving, understandably furious Lunar spouse). A renegade deathknight actively pursuing redemption to reunite with that Lunar love may instead purchase Eternal Vow as the ordinary 3-point Merit, exactly as a Solar would.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-flaw-eternal-vow): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. PRIMARY ABYSSAL ROW: the Merit/Flaw's own header explicitly names "Solars, Lunars and Abyssals only," and its mechanics text gives Abyssal Exalted their own distinct, fully worked-out rule -- the bond typically manifests as a 1-point FLAW for a deathknight (since her former Lunar spouse now rightly regards her with enmity), but a renegade seeking redemption may instead take it as the ordinary 3-point Merit. Both branches are documented in this row's cost field and compatibility text so a player can pick either interpretation depending on whether the character is a loyal deathknight or a renegade.

name: Daredevil
summary: Fortune smiles on the recklessly brave: may reflexively spend one Willpower point to double the rating of a stunt awarded for a Physical action, with a difficulty of 3 or higher.
mechanics: Fortune smiles on the recklessly brave. A character with this Merit may reflexively spend one Willpower point to double the rating of stunt dice awarded to a Physical action with a difficulty of 3 or higher. This Willpower may be spent after the Storyteller determines the rating of a stunt and does not prevent simultaneous Willpower use for automatic success or checking a Virtue. Note that Daredevil does not increase the number of motes or Willpower returned by a successful stunt. Heroic mortals pay one point less for this Merit, as their daring is all the more impressive for its lack of magic. Characters with the Signature Style Merit (see p. 28) do not double the extra die awarded by that Trait in situations where both Merits apply.
compatibility: Any character type; heroic mortals pay one point less, which does not apply to Abyssal Exalted (who pay the full 4-pt. cost as Exalted).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-daredevil): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The discount named is for heroic mortals, not any Exalt type; transfers to Abyssal at the full 4-pt. cost.

name: Brigid's Heir
summary: Brigid's Heir
mechanics: Although a character with this Merit is not necessarily a reincarnation of the apocryphal Mother of All Spells, she walks in the footsteps of Brigid. As a result, she doubles the bonus/experience cost and training time of all Charms and she halves the corresponding costs and training time for spells. Ox-Body Technique is exempt from this doubling, as is any Charm that includes Terrestrial Circle Sorcery as an ultimate prerequisite or leads directly to that Charm. Only beings capable of learning sorcery may purchase this Merit, and Twilight Caste Solars pay one point less than usual. Among Dragon-Blooded sorcerers, this inexplicable attunement to sorcery is called Legacy of Hesiesh.
compatibility: Any character capable of learning sorcery, including Abyssal Exalted, who have confirmed Terrestrial and Celestial Circle Sorcery access per this family's own inventory (Abyssal Solar Circle Sorcery access is confirmed NOT granted, per this family's savant-and-sorcerer coverage, so the 'ultimate prerequisite' exemption for Ox-Body Technique/Terrestrial Circle Sorcery Charms applies the same way it would for any Terrestrial-Circle-capable sorcerer). Twilight Caste Solars pay a reduced 4-pt. cost; that discount does not extend to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-brigids-heir): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal Exalted are eligible for the base 5-pt. version of this Merit since this family's own Terrestrial/Celestial Circle Sorcery access Charms (already inventoried) confirm deathknights can learn sorcery alongside necromancy. The Twilight Caste discount is Solar-specific and does not transfer.

name: Mute
summary: Cannot speak or make vocal utterance of any sort; players describe actions without speech, using sign language, magic, or shared understanding. Higher tiers add physical/vocal-cord damage. Exalted (including Abyssals) pay one point less at every tier.
mechanics: Mute characters may not speak or make vocal utterance of any sort. Their players speak to describe actions, without verbal communication is possible without writing, magic or shared understanding of a sign language. For three points, this limitation has no physiological basis. The character may have lost her voice after exposure to mind-shattering horror, forsaken speech as part of a barbarian taboo or taken a monastic vow of silence. If the character finds her voice or breaks her willing quiet, her player must buy off the Flaw at normal cost. The four-point version of this Flaw involves actual damage to the vocal cords, either as a result of injury or birth defect. Characters incapable of speaking above a faint whisper may purchase this Flaw for one point, regardless of the reason for their quiet. Exalted characters suffering actual silence receive one less point.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) pay one point less at every tier of this Flaw.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-merit-mute): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Note this entry is filed under "Merits" in the source book's Physical Flaw category header despite functioning as a Flaw; transcribed to match the Lunar row's own filing. Cost is reduced by 1 point "for Exalted" generically; Abyssals are Exalted and therefore qualify for the discount.

name: Sterile
summary: Physically incapable of siring or bearing children, whether from accident, illness, or a cruel jest of fate; only worth points for characters who can otherwise enjoy the act of procreation. For an Abyssal, this Flaw forecloses the 4-Resonance-point Litany of Sins trigger for siring/bearing a child with a living lover -- a small, ironic mercy.
mechanics: The character is physically incapable of siring or bearing children. This may be the result of an accident, illness or simply a cruel jest of fate. This Flaw is only worth one point for characters that can still engage in and enjoy the act of procreation. Characters who are also impotent or eunuchs gain two points from the Flaw, corresponding to the expectations of children and the corresponding social stigma against barrenness in the Realm. Dragon-Blooded and mortal Dynasts gain three points from any form of sterility, owing to the expectations of children and the corresponding social stigma against barrenness in the Realm. Members of other cultures who prize fertility on par with the Realm may also receive three points at Storyteller discretion.
compatibility: Any character type; Dragon-Blooded and mortal Dynasts specifically gain the higher 3-pt. value due to Realm social expectations, which does not extend to Abyssal Exalted. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted: this splat's own gaining-resonance row confirms deathknights retain the capacity to sire or bear children with living lovers (itself a listed 4-point Resonance trigger), so Sterile remains a meaningful, if narratively grim, choice -- it removes both the possibility of that particular sin and the family-continuation angle some deathknights might otherwise cling to as a last link to their mortal life.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-sterile): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: cross-referenced to gaining-resonance, since this splat's own rules confirm deathknights can still conceive with living lovers (at a steep Resonance cost) -- Sterile is therefore not merely flavor for an Abyssal, it forecloses a specific documented Resonance risk.

name: Unusual Appearance
summary: Hair/eyes of a striking, unnatural color at 1 point, or fully piebald/colorless (albino) skin and hairlessness at 2 points; the appearance must deviate notably from the local norm to qualify.
mechanics: For one point, the character has hair and/or eyes of a striking color, such as vivid scarlet, sea green, ashen white or some stranger hue. For two points, the character's skin also exhibits remarkable pigmentation or the colorless white of an albino. It is also possible that the character has no hair on his body at all. Regardless of the specifics, the character's appearance must deviate notably from the expected norm to warrant an actual Flaw. Those marked by striking colors have a harder time hiding or impersonating others and may suffer discrimination and suspicious stares from xenophobes (losing one die from pertinent Stealth, Larceny and Social rolls). True albinos often have the Sun-Seared Flaw.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted, and pairs naturally with the Sun-Seared Flaw the same way it does for any character.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-unusual-appearance): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: One Eye
summary: Only a single eye remaining (injury or congenital defect): one-die penalty to Awareness rolls involving distance vision or peripheral vision on the blind side, and increases the difficulty of ranged attacks against the character by one.
mechanics: Whether resulting from injury or congenital defect, characters with this Flaw have only a single eye remaining. This imposes a one-die penalty to Awareness rolls involving distance vision or peripheral vision on the blind side, and increases the difficulty of ranged attacks by one.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-one-eye): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Sun-Seared
summary: Uncomfortable in sunlight, suffering horrible sunburns from relatively mild exposure; common among albinos and the Dune People. THE SOURCE TEXT SPECIFICALLY NAMES GHOSTS AND ABYSSALS as manifesting this trait even more severely (unable to bear light at all), placing them at the most extreme (6-pt.) end of the scale alongside the most tainted spectres and Demon-Blooded.
mechanics: The character finds sunlight uncomfortable and suffers horrible sunburns from relatively mild exposure. This Flaw is common among albinos (see 'Unusual Appearance,' p. 30), especially the Dune People of the South. Some ghosts and Abyssals also manifest this trait at a higher level, unable to bear the light their dead or blackened souls have forsaken. The two-point version of this Flaw is at -1 on all dice pools in direct sunlight and suffer one die of unsoakable bashing damage for each hour of direct exposure. Characters with the three-point version increase the penalty to -2 and suffer damage every 30 minutes. The extreme six-point version of this Flaw is rarely seen outside of the most tainted spectres, Abyssals and Demon-Blooded. Such wretches are at -3 under direct sunlight and suffer one die of unsoakable bashing damage every minute. Characters bundled in heavy clothes or otherwise limiting their direct exposure, such as under an overcast sky or darting from shadow to shadow double the interval necessary to inflict damage. Those with the six-point version only suffer damage every five minutes for indirect exposure.
compatibility: Any character type; the source text names ghosts and Abyssals explicitly as typically manifesting the most severe (6-pt.) tier of this Flaw ("unable to bear the light their dead or blackened souls have forsaken"). One of the most thematically central Flaws in this chapter for a deathknight, whose dead soul quite literally cannot bear the Unconquered Sun's light; a deathknight is free to take any of the three tiers depending on how far her undeath has progressed.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-sun-seared): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. HIGH ABYSSAL RELEVANCE: the source text explicitly names "ghosts and Abyssals" as the two groups who typically manifest this Flaw at its most extreme (6-pt.) tier, tying the effect directly to "the light their dead or blackened souls have forsaken" -- language written specifically with deathknights in mind. No adaptation needed beyond noting the prominence of this fit.

name: Climate Sensitive
summary: Discomfort and penalties outside the character’s accustomed environmental conditions; the point value scales with how common the undesired conditions are to encounter.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw experience discomfort and take ill if they are subjected to environmental conditions substantially different than those they are accustomed to. The value of this Flaw depends on the likelihood of encountering the undesired conditions. For two points, the character responds poorly to a particular extreme of temperature (arctic, tropical) or humidity (arid desert, marsh/jungle). For three points, the character is uncomfortable in any environment lacking these extreme conditions, including temperate climates. Four points indicates the condition that defines the character's home region is specific to a geographical region and cannot be replicated or transplanted without considerable difficulty and expense, such as the pollen of a particular tree or something equally obscure. Whenever a character with this Flaw finds himself in an environment he finds uncomfortable, he adds 1 to the difficulty of all Survival rolls, as well as all Endurance and Resistance rolls to resist manifestations of the undesired conditions. This Flaw may not be taken to any climate the Storyteller indicates the game will visit often.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- a deathknight long-accustomed to the chill of the Underworld could plausibly take this Flaw for discomfort in Creation's warmer regions, or vice versa for one who still clings to living-world comforts.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-climate-sensitive): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Amputee
summary: Missing one or more limbs from congenital defect or later injury; scaled by number/type of limbs lost, with prosthetics/balance rules and Exalted paying a discounted cost at every tier.
mechanics: The character lacks an arm or a leg, either as a result of a congenital defect or injury sustained later in life. Alternately, the character retains the limb, but only as a useless, paralyzed husk. The mechanical effects of amputation vary. Characters missing a hand may not perform two-handed tasks with extreme difficulty, if at all. It is assumed that the character with one hand considers that hand primary and, therefore, suffers no offhand penalty. The loss of both hands means that tasks involving fine dexterity are impossible, though hooks or other prosthetics may allow cruder tasks at a -1 die penalty. Characters may offset the balance penalty with carefully weighted garments, prosthetics or other innovative means (such as tying an object in place for those suffering paralysis). Characters missing an arm can move at half normal movement rate and are at -3 on Athletics rolls involving footwork. Those with a paralyzed leg must also use crutches or drag the paralyzed limb behind them, suffering the same penalties for missing a leg. Characters missing both arms means or perform any tasks requiring manual dexterity without magic, tools or other remarkable means approved by the Storyteller. Characters missing a leg can move at a crutch or peg leg and are at -3 on Athletics rolls involving footwork. Those with a paralyzed leg must also use crutches or drag the paralyzed limb behind them, suffering the same penalties as true amputees. Quadriplegics may not attempt most physical tasks. Such tortured invalids seldom live long in the harsh Age of Sorrows and make poor concepts for the vast majority of players' characters. At best, they may drag themselves painfully and slowly across the ground with their arms. The value of this Flaw is two points for lack of a single arm, three points for a single missing arm or both hands, five points for the loss of any two limbs, seven points for missing eight points for quadriplegics. Fair or not, the gods do not normally make cripples of the Chosen. As with all major physical deformities, Exalted characters receive less compensation for amputation, gaining one less point for losing a single hand or limb and two less points for amputations involving two or more limbs.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) pay a reduced cost at every tier of this Flaw.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-amputee): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Cost is reduced generically "for Exalted" (not naming any particular splat); Abyssals are Exalted and therefore qualify. The source text itself notes some transcription garbling around the exact point-cost list, carried over as-is from Lunar's verified copy since this is universal book text, not an Abyssal-specific concern.

name: Dying
summary: A curse, terminal illness, or other fatal condition that will assuredly kill the character without powerful curative magic; loses a dot of Stamina per interval, dying at Stamina 0.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw suffers from a curse, a terminal illness or other fatal condition and will assuredly perish without the aid of powerful curative magic. The character loses one dot of Stamina per interval, the length of the interval determined by the value of the Flaw. At the lowest level, this period shortens to months for six points and days for ten points. Once a character reaches Stamina 0, he dies. It is always possible to avert this process by some means before returning to full heroic effort, but not without truly heroic effort. This Flaw aids in depicting heroes who strive bravely against all odds or stories rooted in the quest for a cure. Storytellers should feel free to disallow this Flaw without an appropriate story explanation, especially for Exalted characters or a short game.
compatibility: Any character type; the Storyteller is specifically advised to be more cautious allowing this Flaw for Exalted characters, but no splat is excluded outright. For an Abyssal -- already undead -- this Flaw is best reinterpreted as a progressive curse-driven unraveling toward true, final oblivion (the Second Breath the Malfeans threaten oathbreakers with) rather than an ordinary illness, since a deathknight cannot simply 'die' of natural causes the way a mortal or living Exalt can.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-dying): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation flagged in compatibility text: since deathknights are already dead, "Dying" for an Abyssal character is best read as a curse-driven progression toward the character's own final unmaking/oblivion (losing Stamina toward Stamina 0, exactly as written) rather than literal terminal illness -- a judgment call left to Storyteller narration, since the source text does not address undead PCs directly.

name: Small
summary: Stands only four and a half feet tall or less, with a reduced effective Strength for weapon/tool size requirements and one fewer -1 health level.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw stands only four and a half feet tall or less. She has difficulty reaching and manipulating objects designed for normal adult size, reducing her effective Strength by one dot for the sole purpose of meeting the minimum requirements of weapons and large tools. Her reduced size also costs her one -1 health level. In addition to representing children or short adults or pygmy races such as the Djala, this Flaw can aid in portraying extremely gaunt and frail characters of normal height (especially in conjunction with low Stamina).
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted, who do not shapechange the way Lunars do, so the source text's Lunar-only carryover-across-forms clause is not relevant here.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-small): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The Lunar-specific clause about the size reduction carrying across all of a Lunar's shapechanged forms (and its Prey's Skin Disguise cross-reference) was dropped from this row's mechanics text -- Abyssal Exalted have a single fixed body and do not shapechange, so that clause has no Abyssal equivalent.

name: Disfigured
summary: Wretched physical deformity, from concealable scarring/pockmarks (3-pt., Appearance capped at 1) to monstrous full-body horror (4-pt., Appearance 0, automatic social revulsion). THE SOURCE TEXT EXPLICITLY GIVES ABYSSAL EXALTED A VARIANT of this Flaw representing a rotted or death-twisted visage, noting Storytellers may default to the rules in Exalted: The Abyssals itself, which award NO bonus points for the same look.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw suffer some wretched deformity. For three points, they might bear the pitted pockmarks of a smallpox survivor, gross birth defects, heavy scarring from burns or wounds, useless protrusions of Wyld-warped flesh or something stranger still. Exalted and other magical beings may suffer deformities appropriate to their nature, such as a Lunar with a hideous Tell or ghosts with excessively prominent death marks. Characters with the lowest version of the Flaw cannot ever have an Appearance rating greater than 1 and lose one die from other Social pools in which their unsightly deformity could prove a hindrance. It is usually possible to conceal three-point deformities with heavy clothes, masks or other garb. While so attired, the character suffers no penalty and may act as though he has a normal Appearance unless the other party knows his true visage. Characters with Appearance 1 who do not have this Flaw are simply ugly, but not strikingly so. The four-point version of this Flaw represents truly monstrous deformity: full-body scarring, the gaping pits and rotting abscesses of a leper, hideous Wyld-mutation or something even more horrible still. Wretches at this level of hideousness have an Appearance of 0 that cannot be improved with bonus or experience points and automatically fail any Appearance-based roll. All but the most tolerant and charitable souls (Compassion 4+) will respond to the character with utter revulsion and disgust, resulting in a two-die penalty on most Social rolls. At best, monstrous characters can expect contempt and pity. In crueler regions, they may be run out of town or stoned for public amusement. Abyssal Exalted may take this Flaw with Storyteller approval to represent a rotted or death-twisted visage. Storytellers may certainly default to the rules as written in E:Ab, giving no bonus-point reward to players who choose the path of decay and putrescence. However, the game effects of this Flaw adequately represent the fear and loathing a rotted Abyssal will engender in most people.
compatibility: Any character type; the entry names Abyssal Exalted explicitly for a rotted/death-twisted-visage variant, cross-referencing Exalted: The Abyssals (E:Ab) directly. Under the Players Guide's own rules (used by this inventory), a deathknight who takes on that appearance DOES receive bonus points at the normal 3- or 4-pt. rate; a Storyteller may instead default to E:Ab's own version, which awards no points for the same visible decay -- a table-level house-rule choice, not a hard restriction on eligibility.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-disfigured): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. HIGH ABYSSAL RELEVANCE: the source text explicitly states "Abyssal Exalted may take this Flaw with Storyteller approval to represent a rotted or death-twisted visage" and cross-references Exalted: The Abyssals (E:Ab) directly by abbreviation for an alternate, no-bonus-point version of the same concept. Since this inventory uses the Players Guide as the governing text for this chapter, the default ruling here is that a rotted-visage Abyssal DOES receive the normal 3-/4-pt. bonus, with a note that a Storyteller preferring E:Ab's own (bonus-point-free) treatment may substitute it instead.

name: Slow Healing
summary: Mortals with this Flaw heal at half the normal rate; Exalted with this Flaw instead recover at the normal MORTAL rate (rather than their usual superhuman rate), though they still heal perfectly from anything short of amputation given time.
mechanics: Mortal characters with this Flaw recover from injury at half their normal rate. Most such characters do not live long in the brutal Age of Sorrows. Exalted with this Flaw instead recover from their wounds at the rate of normal mortals, but given sufficient time, they still heal perfectly from anything less than amputation.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) have a distinct, milder version of this Flaw (mortal healing rate rather than half-mortal rate) rather than a cost discount.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-slow-healing): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Exalted (generic, including Abyssal) get a distinct effect -- healing at the normal mortal rate instead of the harsher half-mortal-rate mortals suffer -- rather than a point-cost discount. Storytellers running an undead Abyssal PC may reasonably narrate this as unusually sluggish tissue regeneration rather than living convalescence, without changing the mechanic.

name: Weak Immune System
summary: Harder time fighting off illness; mortals add 2 to Endurance/Resistance difficulty vs. disease/infection, while Exalted instead halve their relevant dice pools but keep their usual immunity to the ailment’s actual mechanical effects (discomfort only).
mechanics: Mortal characters with this Flaw have a harder time fighting off illness, their players adding 2 to the difficulty of all Endurance and Resistance rolls for the characters to resist disease and infection. Exalted characters instead half their dice pools to resist or throw off such maladies (rounded down) but retain their usual superhuman resilience to the actual effects of ailments they contract. This means that Chosen with this Flaw will experience the discomfort and distraction of illness for long bouts at a time, perhaps making them wish they were dead even if they are never in any real danger.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) pay a reduced 3-pt. cost and get a milder mechanical variant (halved dice pool, but no loss of their usual immunity to an ailment’s real effects).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-weak-immune-system): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Cost is reduced to 3 points "for Exalted" generically; applies to Abyssals as Exalted.

name: Diminished Attributes
summary: Weaker, slower, less healthy (or, in the Mental/Social variants, less bright/uncouth) bodies than normal adults; grants three points per Physical Attribute dot forfeited during character creation.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw have weaker, slower or less healthy bodies than normal adults. This may be atrophy induced by old age, injury or illness, or perhaps the character is a child who has not developed into full maturity. Regardless, the character receives three points for every Physical Attribute dot forfeited during character creation. Characters cannot use this Flaw to forfeit the free dot they receive in each Attribute, and obviously, may not spend bonus points to purchase Physical Attributes.
