Alternate versions of this Flaw apply to Mental and Social Attributes for characters who are less bright or particularly uncouth. Note that these are considered Mental and Social Flaws rather than falling into the Physical category.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-diminished-attributes): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Diminished Sense
summary: Partial or total loss of a sense; total loss is normally worth three bonus points (two for senses other than sight/hearing), reduced by one if the character has access to a compensating device. Exalted receive one less bonus point per Diminished Sense and may not have more than one sense loss in total.
mechanics: The character suffers partial or total loss of a sense. In the case of partial loss, this Flaw adds 1 to the difficulty of all Awareness rolls based on the dulled sense. This difficulty increase also applies to other rolls determined by the Storyteller, such as Social rolls in a noisy party for hearing loss or long range attacks for vision. Partial loss of a sense is normally worth three bonus points for hearing or vision and two points for other senses. Reduce this value by one if the character has ready access to magic or a device that compensates or corrects for this loss. Glass or crystal spectacles are not unknown in the Realm and the largest cities of the Threshold, although they are often prohibitively expensive (Resources 4 in the Threshold or the rural Realm, Resources 3 in Nexus, the Imperial City or other metropoli, Resources 2 in Chiaroscuro). Total loss of a sense ensures that a character automatically fails any rolls exclusively dependent on that sense, especially Awareness. This loss also adds anywhere from 1 to 3 to the base difficulty of rolls requiring a conjunction of the missing sense and other senses. The Storyteller will impose other penalties as appropriate: Blind characters cannot attack targets beyond 100 yards without magic or an extraordinary stunt and subtract two successes from all attacks and other actions dependent on sight. Deafness makes speech more difficult and requires a Perception + Linguistics roll (difficulty 3+) to lip-read others, making some sort of shared sign language useful. Numbness prevents most pain (halving wound penalties), but the character also cannot discern temperature, feel pleasure or know when she is suffering injury. The value of this Flaw is six points for blindness, four for deafness or numbness and three for loss of smell and taste. The Storyteller may adjust these costs as needed for characters who find ways to circumvent a lost sense or find the loss even more debilitating for some reason. Exalted characters receive one less bonus point per sense for any Diminished Sense, as the gods are loathe to choose people with serious handicaps. No Exalt may have more than one sense loss in its entirety.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) receive one less bonus point per sense and may not stack more than one Diminished Sense.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-diminished-sense): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Cost is reduced by 1 point per sense "for Exalted" generically, with an added cap (no more than one Diminished Sense total) not applied to mortals. Applies to Abyssals as Exalted.

name: Derangement
summary: The curse of madness, drawing from the Exalted core rulebook's derangement list or the book's own suggested forms (Depression, Glossolalia, Hysteria, Sadism); suppressible for a scene with a Willpower point but only curable by magic or lengthy counseling.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw suffers the curse of madness. Perhaps he dallied too close to the warping energies of the Wyld or angered a wrathful spirit or maybe there is no obvious or overt cause. Regardless, his mind suffers regular debilitating bouts of its infirmity. Characters with this Flaw have one of the derangements listed on page 281 of Exalted. It is also possible to suppress the worst effects of this derangement for a scene for a cost of one Willpower point. However, it requires magic or lengthy counseling to actually cure a derangement. The actual game effects of madness are left to your imagination, but the character will probably lose at least two dice from most Social pools with characters who do not share the madness. Characters receive three points for their first derangement and only one point for each subsequent form of madness. Other possible derangements include: Depression (observing or experiencing pain or emotional distress overwhelms the character, causing him to act as though suffering from the Virtue Flaw Heart of Tears, see Exalted, p. 131); Glossolalia (under stress, the character begins speaking loudly in tongues for the rest of the scene; only powerful magic can interpret the meaning of such verbal outbursts, assuming they have any coherence; this derangement primarily manifests in true prophets, shamans and characters with the Whispers Background); Hysteria (under stress, the character lashes out in blind rage as though suffering from the Virtue Flaw Berserk Anger, see Exalted, p. 133); Sadism (with only minor provocation, the character behaves as if constantly suffering from the Virtue Flaw Deliberate Cruelty, see Exalted, p. 132; this also has an effective Compassion rating of 1 until and unless the madness passes, regardless of her true rating).
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- a deathknight’s derangement could as easily stem from the psychic weight of her Exaltation or a Harrowing gone wrong as from any mortal trauma.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-derangement): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Amnesia
summary: Large gaps in the character's memory, from a single missing life event (1 pt.) up to recurring amnesia that prevents remembering anything prior to the last sleep (5 pts.). The source text's special 1-pt. option for Celestial Exalted (Solar/Lunar/Sidereal) who remember nothing of previous incarnations does NOT extend to Abyssal Exalted, whose Exaltation does not work the same way; the base 1/2/5-pt. scale for ordinary lost memories transfers normally.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw suffer large gaps in memory. For one point, the character is missing a notable section of his life (such as childhood) or cannot remember a very crucial event (Exaltation, committing an atrocity). Celestial Exalted who remember absolutely nothing from any previous incarnations of their Exaltation may also purchase Amnesia for one point. For two points, the character remembers nothing from a vast swath of her life: everything before Exaltation, decades spent as a death cultist, etc. For five points, the amnesia is recurring and prevents the character from remembering anything prior to waking up from her last sleep. The character still preserves memory, but cannot access it. Such characters may retain fragmentary memories from before they received the injury or psychic trauma that damaged their mind. Additionally, recurring amnesia prevents characters from learning or advancing Abilities unless they can somehow keep themselves awake or keep a thorough journal. Characters with any version of Amnesia have all their Traits and capabilities, although they often do not know what they can do and certainly do not remember how and when they learned. Likewise, they may find forgotten friends and enemies faintly familiar but may mistake friend for foe and vice versa if the Storyteller feels particularly cruel. Players of amnesiacs should consider letting the Storyteller spend most or all of the character's bonus points to create actual surprises, but this obviously requires a deep level of trust. As an optional rule to encourage suspenseful play, any 'hidden' Traits cost one less bonus point each, but these only emerge when the Storyteller sees fit to reveal them.
compatibility: Any character type at the standard 1-/2-/5-pt. tiers, including Abyssal Exalted -- for example, forgetting an atrocity committed at the moment of Exaltation, or losing whole years spent in her Deathlord's service. The source text's Celestial-Exalted-specific 1-pt. option (for remembering nothing of past-life incarnations) does not apply to Abyssal Exalted, who are not framed as Celestial Exalted and do not reincarnate through new mortal souls the same way. Task's own explicit instruction confirms this Flaw's per-family default is unchanged for the base tiers.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-amnesia): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: the source text's special "Celestial Exalted who remember absolutely nothing from any previous incarnations" 1-pt. clause is scoped to Solar/Lunar/Sidereal and does not extend to Abyssal per this pass's general Celestial-Exalted-exclusion rule; the base Amnesia Flaw (1/2/5 pts. for forgetting real events) transfers normally. Cross-referenced to this splat's own the-title row (loss of one's given name at Exaltation) as a thematically adjacent, though mechanically distinct, form of identity loss every Abyssal already experiences for free.

name: Superstition
summary: A wrong or fanatical idea about something important, treated by the character as sincere fact; scales from a simple personal inconvenience (1 pt.) to a belief that seriously harms others if acted upon (3 pts.).
mechanics: Creation is a magical world where physical laws often a matter of divine whim or are torn asunder by the encroachment of the Wyld or shadowlands. Strange local beliefs and customs are very often real and meaningful -- and perhaps even necessary. Unfortunately, characters with this Flaw hold a wrong or fanatical idea about something important. Perhaps this erroneous belief was once rooted in fact or a kernel of truth, but that time is long past. The value of this Flaw depends on the deviation and danger of the character's superstitious beliefs. For one point, the custom is simply inconvenient. The character might believe that road spirits abhor travelers who walk in a straight line down their path or that a certain livestock animal is inherently unclean and therefore unsuitable for human consumption. At two points, the superstition is actually dangerous to oneself (or to others who believe it). The character may think that garlic repels the undead or put faith in a medicine that does nothing against harm. Three-point versions of this Flaw involve harm to others. Characters may seriously believe the year will not return from the chaos of Calibration unless they receive a dedicated sacrifice of a virgin, or they may believe that anyone who commits adultery must die by public stoning. Exercise of such beliefs they are not the law of the land may get a character in trouble with the authorities or incur retaliation. Characters who discover and come to accept the falsehood of their superstitions must buy off this Flaw for experience. Characters receive one less point for this Flaw if the game will take place mostly in areas where the belief is commonly held.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-superstition): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Vice
summary: A moral weakness, sin, or failing that tempts the character above all others (e.g. lust for the living, carnal cruelty, bigotry); when relevant, the character loses two dice from the affected Virtue for every point invested and may indulge in it over better judgment. This Flaw may not alter or ameliorate an Abyssal's Resonance or the Abyssal Curse.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw suffers a particular sin or failing that tempts him above all others. A warrior of great Valor may harbor a secret fear of the undead. A monk who masters ascetic Temperance may yet fall to the lure of carnal desire. Those of great Conviction may find their implacable confidence shattered when they must assume a position of leadership. Deep Compassion may mask a streak of bigotry and cruelty toward a group of people or an utter disinterest in romance. In situations relevant to the sinful condition, the character loses two dice from the affected Virtue for every point invested in the Vice. This may reduce the dice pool of a Virtue to zero, in which case the character automatically indulges in the sin and immoderation of his Vice over the better judgment of his morality. Characters may not have more than one Vice. Instead, those with deep moral deficiencies are Callous (see p. 35). This Flaw may not alter or ameliorate an Abyssal's Resonance or the Abyssal Curse, and Storytellers should ban any Vice that obviously attempts to circumvent this restriction.
compatibility: Any character type; for Abyssal Exalted, this Flaw is explicitly barred from altering or ameliorating Resonance or the Abyssal Curse (this splat's own Great-Curse analog), mirroring the source text's original restriction against altering the Great Curse for Solar/Lunar/Sidereal characters.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-vice): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: the source text's restriction ("This Flaw may not alter or ameliorate the Great Curse") was rewritten for this row to reference Resonance/the Abyssal Curse -- this splat's own Great-Curse analog (per the resonance and abyssal-curse rows) -- rather than the Great Curse Solar/Lunar/Sidereal characters suffer.

name: Addiction
summary: An addiction to some substance, scaling 1-3 points by legality/danger/expense, +1 if Resources can't support the habit, +2 if it consumes the character's entire life. Exalted subtract from the addiction rating owing to hardier constitutions.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw suffer an addiction to some substance, without which they suffer the discomfort -- and perhaps danger -- of withdrawal. For one point, this substance is relatively easy and legal to obtain, inexpensive enough that the habit will not bankrupt the character and reasonably safe barring excessive overdose. Examples include alcohol, qat and marijuana. For two points, the substance is more serious due to rarity or more debilitating side effects. Examples include opium, rasp spider venom and ice fern spores. Three-point addictions are expensive and/or dangerous, such as rock cocaine, heroin and bright morning. Add one to the value of an addiction if the character's Resources cannot support regular use. Add two if the character cannot possibly afford a single dose and must turn to theft or deep debt or if the addiction controls the character's entire life. Exalted subtract one from the rating of their addictions, owing to their hardier constitutions. Actual effects of addiction and withdrawal depend on the drug and Storyteller discretion but may include dice penalties, damage or rolls to remain conscious. Thorough information on the drug trade and most of the example drugs can be found in Chapter Two of Manacle and Coin.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) subtract one from their addiction's rating owing to hardier constitutions. The source text's separate Wyld-addiction variant is cross-referenced to Exalted: The Lunars p. 205, which is specific to that splat and does not apply here; a deathknight's own exotic addictions (feeding via anima-formed fangs, an unhealthy craving for the Malfeans' whispers, etc.) would use this Flaw's general framework at Storyteller discretion instead.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-addiction): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: the source text's direct cross-reference to Exalted: The Lunars p. 205 for Wyld-addiction rules was dropped from this row's mechanics text since it is Lunar-specific and has no Abyssal equivalent; the Exalted-generic 1-point discount for hardier constitutions was retained since it applies to Abyssals as Exalted.

name: Callous
summary: Selfish pragmatism over scruples and integrity; gains two bonus points per point of Virtue forfeited during character creation, cannot start with a Willpower rating more than one point higher than the sum of the two highest Virtues, and cannot have the Paragon Nature.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw believes in selfish pragmatism over scruples and integrity. He gains two bonus points for every dot of Virtues his player forfeits during character creation. Callous characters cannot forfeit their last dot of a Virtue and may not begin play with a Willpower rating more than one point higher than the sum of their two highest Virtues. This limit applies until such a time as the character has a total of 9 dots of Virtues, at which point the character automatically loses this Flaw at no cost. Thus, a monstrous, intemperate, inconstant coward with a rating of 1 in all Virtues could never have a Willpower higher than 3. Characters with this Flaw may not have the Paragon Nature. Exalted with this Flaw suffer Virtue Flaws appropriate to their highest Virtue, if applicable.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) with this Flaw suffer the standard Exalted Virtue Flaw tied to their highest Virtue, framed through this splat's own Virtues of Death (a Callous deathknight's Virtue dots are still Compassion/Conviction/Temperance/Valor, just redefined per the virtues-of-death row) -- also cross-referenced by the Weak-Willed Flaw's Willpower-minimum exception.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-callous): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Cross-referenced to this splat's own virtues-of-death row (in place of a Lunar-specific cross-reference) since an Abyssal's Virtue Flaw and Virtue dots are interpreted through that framework. Also cross-references True Paragon (this Flaw and that Merit remain mutually exclusive for Abyssal characters same as any other splat).

name: Nightmares
summary: Horrific dreams whenever the character sleeps, adding 1 to the difficulty of regaining Willpower via Conviction after sleep, and inflicting lingering one-die penalties and unsoakable bashing damage on a botched Conviction roll.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw experiences horrific dreams whenever she sleeps. She may have experienced a mind-shattering personal trauma or received the attention of malefic spirits or sorcerers, or perhaps she harbors guilt over past misdeeds. Regardless, she finds little solace in slumber and adds 1 to the difficulty to regain Willpower with Conviction after sleep. If the Conviction roll botches, the character loses one point of temporary Willpower and is plagued with lingering horror for the rest of the day, resulting in a one-die penalty to all non-reflexive actions.
compatibility: Any character type; ghosts get a distinct mechanical variant (Slumber-healing roll instead of Willpower-regain roll) that does not apply to Abyssal Exalted, since deathknights are not Ghosts in the game's technical sense -- they use the standard Willpower-regain-via-Conviction-after-sleep mechanic like any living Exalt.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-nightmares): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. The source text's ghost-specific variant (a distinct being type from Abyssal Exalted) was dropped from this row's mechanics text; a deathknight uses the standard Conviction-based Willpower-regain mechanic.

name: Pacifist
summary: Cannot bring himself to fight, adding 1 to the difficulty of attacks (3-pt.), or cannot attack anyone at all without spending a Willpower point to overcome his aversion for a scene (5-pt.).
mechanics: However noble in intent, pacifism carries great risks in the violent, imperfect reality of the Age of Sorrows. Those who will not fight must find protectors who will or suffer at the hands of those less idealistically principled. For three points, a pacifist adds 1 to the difficulty of her attacks. Even retaliation or combat in self-defense carries this penalty, as the character's peaceful nature rebels against the very notion of inflicting harm. Characters with the five-point version of this Flaw may not attack anyone without the expenditure of a Willpower point to overcome her aversion to violence for a scene. Even if they do take violent action out of necessity, such characters add 1 to the difficulty of their attacks.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted, particularly a renegade deathknight clinging to what remains of her mortal conscience.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-pacifist): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Unskilled
summary: Less education and training than most adults, from youth, dementia, or lack of practice; grants one bonus point per Ability dot forfeited during character creation, though known Favored Abilities must still meet minimum statistical requirements (one dot for Exalted).
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw have less education and training to draw upon than most adults. They may be too young to know much yet or so old that dementia and lack of practice has robbed them of their skill. Perhaps he slept through school, or maybe they just aren't the sharpest knives in the drawer (reflected by low Intelligence or Wits). Whatever the reason, such a character receives one bonus point for every dot of Abilities forfeited during character creation. Characters with this Flaw must still meet the statistic requirements of all known Favored Abilities (one dot for Exalted; all Favored Abilities must equal or above non-Favored for mortals) and obviously cannot purchase Ability dots with bonus points.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) must still keep at least one dot in any known Favored Ability despite this Flaw.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-unskilled): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Minor Exalted-specific requirement (one dot minimum in Favored/Caste Abilities), not an exclusion; applies to Abyssals as Exalted.

name: Weak-Willed
summary: Gnawing self-doubt and lack of drive; grants one bonus point per dot of permanent Willpower forfeited during character creation, extremely uncommon among the Chosen. Exalted with this Flaw may not begin with Willpower lower than 4 unless also Callous, in which case (or if UnExalted) Willpower can be as low as 2.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw suffers gnawing self-doubt and lack of drive. She may have experienced the hunger of a Fair One or had her mind shattered by wicked sorcery. Or maybe she's simply a pathetic wretch. Regardless, the character gains one bonus point for every dot of permanent Willpower her player forfeits during character creation. This Flaw is extremely uncommon among the Chosen, as the Celestines do not Exalt spiritual weaklings. Only Exalted who suffered Willpower loss since their Exaltation may take this Flaw and only with a remarkable story explanation. Exalted characters with this Flaw may not begin with a Willpower rating lower than 4, unless they are also Callous (see p. 35). UnExalted and Callous Exalted characters may have a Willpower score as low as 2.
compatibility: Any character type; Exalted (including Abyssal Exalted) face a floor of Willpower 4 for this Flaw unless also Callous, and it is explicitly stated to be extremely rare for any Exalt to take (requiring a story reason for post-Exaltation Willpower loss).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-weak-willed): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Generic Exalted-only restriction and floor (Willpower 4 minimum, or 2 if also Callous); applies to Abyssals as Exalted, but the text stresses this combination is extremely uncommon and needs a story justification -- for a deathknight, perhaps a Harrowing gone catastrophically wrong.

name: Barbarian
summary: Grew up outside the bounds of civilization and does not know the ways of soft city-dwellers; loses one die from all Social dice pools related to understanding or expressing civilized etiquette, and is not assumed literate unless Lore 2+.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw grew up outside the bounds of civilization and do not know the ways of soft city-dwellers. Such individuals lose one die from all Social dice pools related to understanding or expressing civilized etiquette and are not assumed to be literate unless they have Lore 2 or more. Players playing a barbarian-only game may not take this Flaw unless they interact with civilization on a fairly regular basis in a capacity that makes their upbringing a liability.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-barbarian): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged.

name: Secrets
summary: The character harbors a secret that could prove embarrassing or dangerous if others learn of it, scaling from mild embarrassment (1 pt.) up to deadly, death-penalty-worthy crimes/heresies (3 pts.).
mechanics: The character harbors a secret that could prove embarrassing or even dangerous if others were to learn of it. The value of this Flaw depends on the severity of the affair. For one point, it is something highly inconvenient or humiliating, like a bastard child from an illicit affair. The character's reputation and relationships may suffer, but no harm will befall him if word gets out. For two points, the secret is more serious and will certainly lead to reprisal if it comes to light. Criminals who have gotten away with their crimes have this level of Secrets, as do Anathema living in the Imperial City. Three-point secrets are deadly serious affairs. If the authorities find out, it will mean death or a comparably unpleasant fate. This level is the purview of traitors, cannibals, assassins and those who commit the most heinous and depraved acts. Secrets of greater value may exist, but these outrageous blasphemies are left wholly to the demented imaginations of players and Storytellers.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific variant is given, though "Anathema living in the Imperial City" is used as a flavor example of a 2-pt. secret -- Anathema is the Realm's term for any Exalted outside the Dragon-Blooded, including Abyssals, and a deathknight infiltrator hiding in plain sight among the living is a strong fit for this Flaw at any tier.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-secrets): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged. The "Anathema living in the Imperial City" flavor example directly suits a deathknight spy or infiltrator concept.

name: Disciple
summary: The character's superiors have entrusted her with a student she must train and look after, unable to abandon the relationship without permission from a higher-ranking authority; scales 1-5 points by the disciple's demands on the character's time and the consequences of the disciple's misbehavior.
mechanics: The character's superiors have entrusted her with a student that she must train and look after. In effect, the character is the mentor of her pupil, save that she cannot abandon the relationship without permission from those higher ranking than her. The student has the potential to become as powerful as the character, given time and experience. The value of this Flaw depends on the cooperativeness of the disciple and the level of obligation/contact required, ranging from a cooperative disciple requiring minimal attention (one point) to a teacher's nightmare of an insipid, cloying wretch or willfully malicious terror (five points). Should a character fail in her teaching duties, unpleasant consequences invariably follow. The disciple may be given a worse disciple as an object lesson or may temporarily be stripped of rank (losing dots of Backing, Command, Liege or other status-based Backgrounds as appropriate). This Flaw is particularly common among Sidereals and Immaculates, both of whom depend on a rigid hierarchy for training.
compatibility: Any character type; the book notes this Flaw is particularly common among Sidereals and Immaculates due to their rigid training hierarchies, but Abyssal Exalted fit just as naturally: a Deathlord who assigns a junior deathknight to an established one for training is a direct analog, and consequences for a failed disciple could reduce the mentor's own Liege standing.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-disciple): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific reinterpretation: this row's mechanics text explicitly folds in the Liege Background (already named generically in the source as one possible status-Background consequence) as the natural Abyssal hook for this Flaw -- a Deathlord assigning a deathknight a disciple mirrors the Sidereal/Immaculate hierarchy the source text calls out as this Flaw's most common home.

name: Enemy/Rival
summary: The character has earned the enmity of an individual or group; functions as a reverse Allies Background, with a point value matching the power of the character’s foes -- up to a Deathlord, First Age survivor, or Third Circle fetch at five points.
mechanics: The character has earned the enmity of an individual or group. This Flaw functions like a reverse of the Allies Background, with a corresponding point value matching the power of the character's foes. Thus, two enemies equivalent to starting characters would award two points, as would a more experienced adversary. At five points, the character might contend with the wrath of a powerful god, a Deathlord, an Exalted survivor of the First Age, a Third Circle fetich or a similarly potent being. The only difference between a rival and an enemy is that the former is a member of an organization to which the character belongs, but the underlying nature of the animosity and adversity remains the same, but neither the rival nor the character may openly act against the other without professional reprisal from their organization. Thus, a rival represents a more subtle enemy, one that cannot overcome with brute force alone.
compatibility: Any character type; the five-point tier’s flavor examples (a Deathlord, a First Age survivor, a Third Circle fetch) are setting-color, not eligibility restrictions. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted -- a deathknight’s enemy could be a Wyld Hunt strike team, a rival deathknight, or even her own Deathlord grown suspicious of her loyalty.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-enemy-rival): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged. Since the Celestial-Exalted-only Known Anathema Flaw was excluded from this pass (its header does not extend to Abyssal), this generic Enemy/Rival Flaw is the natural stand-in for representing a deathknight's Wyld Hunt or Immaculate Order pursuers.

name: Wanted
summary: The character is a known criminal or has otherwise incurred the wrath of authorities willing to send hunters after her, regardless of actual guilt; scales from a minor crime like an escaped slave or defaulted loan (1 pt.) to inherent treason such as consorting with the Deathlords, fleeing rebellion, or assassinating a king (5 pts.).
mechanics: The character is a known criminal, or her actions have somehow incurred the wrath of authorities willing to send hunters after her. Whether or not she is actually innocent is irrelevant. For one point, the character is most likely an escaped slave or has defaulted on a moderate loan, committed a theft or become involved in some other minor crime involving another's property. Pursuit will be slight if at all, though the character will need to keep a low profile if she ever returns home. Three points indicates a murder or violent crime and a certainty of pursuit, most likely leading to death or lengthy imprisonment. Five points indicates the character has committed an act of inherent inexcusable treason: consorting with the Deathlords or fleeing a rebellion, assassinating the king, etc. Storytellers should use these guidelines to interpolate crimes rated at two or four points.
compatibility: Any character type; the five-point tier’s flavor example ("consorting with the Deathlords") is setting-color for the severity of treason, not an eligibility restriction. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-wanted): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; selectable for Abyssal at any point tier.

name: Disturbing
summary: The character makes others uncomfortable through an indefinable aura of menace (not necessarily ugliness or rudeness), adding 1 (2 pts.) or 2 (3 pts.) to the difficulty of all Social rolls not based on intimidation, and causing most people to give the character a wide berth.
mechanics: Characters with this Flaw make others uncomfortable. It's not that they are necessarily ugly or even rude, but they exude an indefinable aura of menace that discomfits those around them. For two points, this adds 1 to the difficulty of all Social rolls not based on intimidation. For three points, this penalty increases to 2. In general, characters with this Flaw can expect most people to give them a wide berth and to minimize contact even when Social rolls do not actually come into play.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific restriction noted. Worth weighing against this splat's own Resonance Trait for an Abyssal character, since Resonance already imposes a similar (though separately-tracked) Social penalty as its rating climbs -- Storytellers should treat Disturbing as a fixed baseline unease distinct from, and additive with, Resonance's fluctuating aura rather than double-counting the same narrative beat twice without acknowledging it.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-disturbing): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Abyssal-specific note: cross-referenced to this splat's own resonance row, since Resonance already inflicts a similar Social penalty as it rises -- both can coexist (a deathknight can be innately Disturbing on top of Resonance-driven unease) but a Storyteller should be aware the two stack for a high-Resonance, Disturbing deathknight.

name: Child
summary: The character has not yet reached full maturity; most adults treat him with patronizing amusement or disdain and generally ignore his opinions, costing 1-3 dice on Social rolls involving interactions with adults. Most children also have the Small Flaw and a measure of Unskilled.
mechanics: The character has not yet reached full maturity, and therefore, most adults treat him with patronizing amusement or disdain. His opinions are generally ignored in favor of those older or wiser, especially in matters for his own good. And that assumes anyone even bothers to hear what he has to say in the first place. The character's player loses one to three dice from all Social rolls involving interactions with adults, depending on the tolerance of the adult in question. Most children also have the Small Frame (see p. 32) and a measure of Unskilled (see p. 36).
compatibility: Any character type; a young Exalt could take this Flaw, though it is most relevant to characters who Exalt or begin play at a young age. Unusual, but not textually prohibited, for an Abyssal: the Deathlords generally seek out mortals of proven capability rather than children, but a Storyteller running an especially dark story could allow it.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-child): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; flagged in compatibility text as an unusual (but not prohibited) concept for a Deathlord-chosen Abyssal, since Deathlords typically favor proven, capable mortals rather than children.

name: Damaged Artifact
summary: An Artifact owned through the Artifact Background has suffered damage that impairs its function, scaling from minor damage (1 pt.) up to near-total damage (3 pts., artifact presently useless but repairable). Points gained cannot exceed the Background/bonus points spent obtaining the artifact -- and THE SOURCE TEXT'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE USES AN ABYSSAL CHARACTER, cross-referencing this splat's altered Artifact Background costs directly (E:Ab p. 131).
mechanics: One of the mystical wonders owned by the character through purchase of the Artifact Background has suffered damage, either in the distant past or since it has fallen into her possession. The extent of this damage and the effect of that damage on the artifact's ability to function correctly depend on the number of points invested in this Flaw. One point indicates minor damage. A weapon may lose a point of damage or accuracy or some other characteristic, while armor loses an equivalent number of points from its lethal and bashing soak or other ratings. Two points indicates major damage, costing five points from weapons and armor or resulting in half effectiveness or half consistency from complicated devices. Three points indicates near-total damage. The artifact is presently useless, though it may be repaired. Players may not gain more points from this Flaw than the rating of Background and/or bonus points spent obtaining the artifact, whichever is less. Characters must have at least one more point of Artifact than the points obtained with this Flaw. The Solar craftsman Velgash found tattered wings of the raptor in a tomb (see BoTC, p. 95). Using the Artifact Background available to Solars, Velgash's player had to spend four points to obtain this artifact. He may thus gain the full three points from Damaged Artifact to represent a presently useless pair of wings. However, if the Abyssal tomb robber Clutching Owl began play with the same tattered wings, he could not receive more than two points from their condition, since it would cost only two points to obtain the wings with the Abyssal version of the Artifact Background (see E:Ab, p. 131).
compatibility: Any character type with an Artifact Background, including Abyssal Exalted. This splat's altered Artifact Background uses a tier table rather than a direct dots-to-rating conversion (per this family's own artifact-background-altered row: 1 dot = combined rating ≤ 3, 2 dots ≤ 5, 3 dots ≤ 7, 4 dots ≤ 10, 5 dots ≤ 13), so an Abyssal's Damaged Artifact cap should be read against that tier table's combined-rating ceiling for the dot level actually spent, exactly as the source text's own Clutching Owl example computes (2 Background points bought access up to combined rating 5, capping Damaged Artifact at 2 points for an item that would otherwise cost more for a Solar under the standard Background).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-damaged-artifact): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. PRIMARY ABYSSAL ROW: the source text's own worked example uses an Abyssal character ("the Abyssal tomb robber Clutching Owl") and explicitly cross-references Exalted: The Abyssals p. 131 for this splat's altered Artifact Background costs. Cross-referenced to this family's own artifact-background-altered row (which documents the actual 1-5 dot tier table) so a Storyteller can apply this Flaw's Background-cost cap correctly against Abyssal's non-standard Artifact Background math rather than the core-Exalted per-dot system the source text otherwise assumes.

name: Debt
summary: The character owes money or goods to an individual or organization of substantial power (e.g. a wealthy Dynast or the Guild), functioning as an inverse Resources Background with an identical rating system; failure to make scheduled payments brings hunters, militia, or worse.
mechanics: The character owes money or goods to an individual or organization of substantial power, such as a wealthy Dynast or even the Guild itself. The character must either pay regular installments with interest or promise a full repayment as of a certain date agreed upon by both parties. If the character fails to meet her obligations on schedule, unpleasant consequences will follow. This Flaw functions as an inverse of the Resources Background with an identical rating system. Thus, a character with four points of Debt owes a sum equal to Resources 4. It is possible for characters to have both Debt and Resources, provided the former exceeds the latter. Players who buy off Debt with Resources accumulated in play or borrowed from another lender do not need to spend experience points to do so.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific restriction noted. Applicable to Abyssal Exalted using the standard, unaltered Resources Background; a deathknight's creditor could equally be a mortal patron, a ghost broker, or even her own Deathlord (functioning similarly to an inverse of the Liege Background's bonus points, at Storyteller discretion).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-debt): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; transfers to Abyssal unchanged using the standard core-Exalted Resources Background.

name: Unbidden Oracle
summary: At least once per story but no more than once per scene, the character unintentionally speaks prophetic words of ill omen, invariably at the most inopportune moment; such prophecies almost always come true. A point of Willpower can be spent to prevent an outburst.
mechanics: At least once per story, but no more than once per scene, a character with this Flaw speaks prophetic words of ill omen without meaning to. Such outbursts invariably come at the most inopportune or impolitic moment. Prophecies obtained from this Flaw almost always come true -- or would come true if the blurted warning didn't prompt countermeasures. Only rarely will an unbidden oracle speak of his own impending misfortune. Players may prevent a prophetic outburst by spending a point of Willpower, but prophecies of any importance will find their way into the oracle's mouth eventually.
compatibility: Any character type, including Abyssal Exalted; no eligibility restriction. For a deathknight, these outbursts could plausibly be reframed as the Malfeans' own whispers leaking involuntarily through her Resonance-tainted Essence, a darker mirror of the more controlled insight this splat's Whispers Background grants on purpose.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-unbidden-oracle): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction. The source text's own flavor tie to the (Sidereal-administered) Bureau of Destiny was dropped as not relevant to Abyssal; cross-referenced instead to this splat's own Whispers Background as the closer thematic parallel -- an uncontrolled, cursed echo of that Background's deliberate insight.

name: Dark Fate
summary: No matter how heroic her deeds, the character will ultimately suffer or bring about some great tragedy at its appointed time, defying even the Maidens' intervention; severity scales from a lifetime of petty miseries or a painful demise (1 pt.) to epic, empire-crumbling catastrophe (5 pts.). THE SOURCE TEXT EXPLICITLY STATES the fate of the dead and Abyssals is written in the stars of the UNDERWORLD rather than Creation, and that not even the Maidens can change those destinies.
mechanics: No happy ending awaits a character with Dark Fate. No matter how heroic and glorious her destiny and deeds, she shall ultimately suffer or bring about some great tragedy at its appointed time, defying the most potent sorcery, astrology and divine intervention short of the Maidens themselves. The specifics of a given doom may vary widely in severity depending on the number of points invested in this Flaw, from a one-point violent demise or lifetime of petty miseries up to a five-point epic catastrophe that can crumble entire empires. Those fated for ruin seldom know the curse they bear, though ill portents of varying intensity typically accompany their birth or Exaltation. Any astrologer can sense the presence of doom in the horoscope of such individuals with a single success (see Exalted, p. 251). Identifying the specifics of a Dark Fate is much harder and never certain (minimum difficulty 5). As always, the fate of the dead and Abyssals live written in the stars of the Underworld rather than the stars of Creation, and not even the Maidens can change those destinies. Ironically, those cursed with Dark Fate receive the same coincidental protection as those with Destiny (see p. 25). They will survive to meet their doom healthy and happy. Celestial Exalted with this Flaw often pass similar dooms on to the next souls who bear their Essence. Sidereal Exalted are normally exempt from Dark Fate on account of their position in the Bureau of Destiny.
compatibility: Any character type EXCEPT Sidereals normally, per the source text's exemption for their Bureau of Destiny role. Abyssal Exalted face no such restriction and are fully eligible at any point tier -- indeed, the source text explicitly confirms an Abyssal's Dark Fate is written into the Underworld's own stars rather than Creation's, immune even to the Maidens' intervention, a striking and thematically rich fit for this splat.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-dark-fate): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. HIGH ABYSSAL RELEVANCE: the source text explicitly names Abyssals ("the fate of the dead and Abyssals live written in the stars of the Underworld") as having their own distinct fate-tracking cosmology for this Flaw, unreachable even by the Maidens. No splat-specific restriction bars Abyssal eligibility (only Sidereals are normally exempted, for an unrelated reason). Cross-references the Destiny Merit, this splat's own equally Abyssal-explicit companion Trait.

name: Unlucky
summary: The character suffers an endless stream of purposeless misfortune (unlike Dark Fate, this has no ultimate destiny behind it). The Storyteller gets a negative luck pool equal to points invested, spendable to force rerolls of the character's rolls (keeping the worse result) or to negatively bias games of chance; the pool refreshes at the end of every story.
mechanics: A character with this Flaw suffers an endless stream of misfortune that plagues his life. Such misfortune is not the same as a Dark Fate (see p. 39) in that it has no ultimate purpose. Chance simply dislikes the character and thwarts his enterprises. The character receives a negative luck pool equal to the points invested in the Flaw. The Storyteller may spend a point of this bad luck to force the reroll of any roll on the part of the character's player at the same difficulty and target number as the original roll. The least successful result of these applies unless the character spends additional points of bad luck to force another reroll and so on until the Storyteller runs out of luck or accepts the outcome of the lowest roll. Alternately, the Storyteller may spend points of bad luck to negatively influence a game of chance or other completely random event involving the character. Used in such fashion, the Storyteller rolls one die, subtracting one from the result for every luck point spent. If this yields a result of 5 or less, the outcome opposes the character. Strangely enough, characters may be simultaneously Lucky (see p. 27) and Unlucky. Although the two can cancel (particularly in contests of chance), the Storyteller and the player would not spend their respective luck points to affect the same rolls. A character blessed with mixed fortune experiences great highs and lows without any mediocrity, winning a king's ransom in a game and losing it the next night. Characters with this Flaw refresh their pool of bad luck at the end of every story.
compatibility: Any character type; no splat-specific restriction noted. Fully applicable to Abyssal Exalted, and can stack with the Lucky Merit (a deathknight can be simultaneously blessed and cursed, per the source text).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-unlucky): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No splat-specific eligibility restriction; selectable for Abyssal at any point tier. Distinct from the Dark Fate Flaw -- Unlucky has no destined purpose, just a spendable Storyteller-controlled bad-luck pool.

name: Permanent Caste Mark
summary: LUNAR'S NOTES ALREADY FLAGGED THIS ROW FOR THE ABYSSAL FOLLOW-UP: an Exalt with this Flaw always displays his Caste Mark on his brow even without spending Essence. For an Abyssal, the mark is a fierce brand charred and stained to inky black rather than a colored tattoo -- widely recognized (via Immaculate Order teaching, alongside the Solar and Lunar marks) as a sign of Anathema.
mechanics: An Exalt with this Flaw always displays his Caste Mark on his brow. The mark does not glow without expenditure of Essence, normally appearing as a tattoo of the appropriate color: gold for Solars, silver for Lunars and the color of a Sidereal's patron Maiden. The Caste Mark of an Abyssal is a fierce brand charred and stained to inky black. Due to the widespread teachings of the Immaculate Order, many individuals in Creation recognize the symbols of the Solars, the Lunars and the Abyssals as signs of Anathema. People who behold such marks will respond appropriately. Sidereal marks are far less known and, therefore, are worth only one point, though still unusual enough to draw attention. It is relatively easy to veil a Caste Mark, at least until it begins to glow.
compatibility: Restricted by the Merit/Flaw's own header to "Celestial Exalted only" as written, but the mechanics text explicitly and separately describes an Abyssal version ("The Caste Mark of an Abyssal is a fierce brand charred and stained to inky black") and includes Abyssals among the marks the Immaculate Order teaches people to recognize as Anathema -- per this pass's own rule, an explicit body-text carve-out overrides the narrower header framing. Abyssals pay the same 2-pt. cost as Solars and Lunars (whose marks are equally widely recognized), not the reduced 1-pt. Sidereal tier.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-permanent-caste-mark): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. INCLUDED DESPITE THE "CELESTIAL EXALTED ONLY" HEADER because the body text explicitly defines an Abyssal Caste Mark variant (a charred black brand) and folds Abyssals into the Immaculate Order's Anathema-recognition list alongside Solars and Lunars -- Lunar's own transcription flagged this exact header-vs-body inconsistency as a note for this Abyssal follow-up pass. Cost is the standard 2-pt. tier (no reduced-cost exception is given for Abyssals, unlike Sidereals).

name: Beacon of Power
summary: Exalted with this Flaw cannot hide their divinity: they have only a single Essence pool (Personal + Peripheral combined), all of which counts as Peripheral for anima-display purposes, greatly increasing the risk of revealing themselves as Anathema. Costs the same 4 points for all Exalt types, but Solar Night Caste and ABYSSAL DAY CASTE Exalted may not take it.
mechanics: Exalted with this Flaw cannot hide their divinity. Such characters have only a single Essence pool equal to the sum of their Personal and Peripheral Essence, all of which is considered Peripheral for the purposes of anima displays. This Flaw costs the same for Exalted of all types. Night and Day Caste Exalted may not take this Flaw.
compatibility: Open to Exalted of all types (not mortals/other beings) at the same flat 4-point cost regardless of splat. Explicitly BARRED for Day Caste Abyssals (whose entire caste concept is built around subtlety and concealment) and Solar Night Caste, per the source text's "Night and Day Caste Exalted may not take this Flaw" restriction. Dusk, Midnight, Daybreak, and Moonshadow Caste Abyssals may take this Flaw normally at the standard 4-pt. cost.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-beacon-of-power): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. Lunar's own transcription flagged this exact ambiguity for the Abyssal follow-up: "'Day' does not match any Lunar caste and most likely refers to the Abyssal Day Caste." CONFIRMED against this family's own inventory -- Day is one of the five Abyssal Castes (per the day-caste row) -- so this Flaw's caste-based exclusion applies directly and specifically to Day Caste deathknights; the other four Abyssal Castes may take it normally.

name: Weak Essence
summary: The character suffers stunted magical development (or recently received Exaltation), reducing starting Essence rating to 1 and severely limiting Charm selection. New Exalts may withhold up to five Charms in reserve (waiving their experience cost but not training time) until Essence can be raised in play.
mechanics: Individuals with this Flaw suffer stunted magical development, or perhaps they only recently received Exaltation. This circumstance reduces the character's starting Essence rating to 1, severely limiting Charm selection. If used to represent a new Exalt, the player may choose to withhold up to five Charms in reserve (typically until after the character can raise Essence in play). Withheld Charms waive their experience cost, though they still require the same training time. Other magical beings may take this Flaw, provided that they normally have a starting Essence of 2. Dragon Kings are an exception to this rule, since those with Essence 1 are feral predators unsuitable for players.
compatibility: Available to any newly-Exalted character of any splat (including Abyssal Exalted) starting at Essence 1 instead of the usual starting Essence of 2. Also available to other magical beings whose baseline starting Essence is 2, EXCEPT Dragon Kings (whose Essence-1 form is a feral, non-player-suitable predator).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-weak-essence): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. No Abyssal-specific restriction; a newly-Exalted deathknight may take this Flaw to start at Essence 1 rather than this splat's normal starting Essence of 2 (per abyssal-character-creation-overview), withholding up to five Charms (no experience cost, but full training time still required) until Essence is raised in play.

name: Death-Taint
summary: ABYSSAL-CENTRAL FLAW: some Abyssal Exalted feel the Malfeans' curse more keenly, gaining 4 bonus points but altering the Abyssal Curse's Resonance mechanics -- whenever Resonance pool exceeds 10, it resets to zero and the character gains a point of permanent Resonance (capped at Essence). Ghosts with this Flaw instead suffer tainted Passions via the Whisper of Oblivion.
mechanics: Some Abyssal Exalted feel the touch of the Malfeans' displeasure and accursed power more keenly than others. This deepened taint provides four bonus points and alters the mechanics of the Abyssal Curse. Whenever the character's Resonance pool exceeds a rating of 10, her pool resets to zero, and she gains a point of permanent Resonance. Permanent Resonance is cumulative with temporary Resonance in determining social penalties and Virtue difficulties, and it also adds its rating to the power of any evoked or unintentional Resonance effects. Characters may not have a permanent Resonance higher than their Essence. Any Resonance Breaks after this limit merely evoke dark miracles with a rating equal to the excess, as with most Abyssals. Characters wishing to reduce their permanent Resonance by one dot must spend five experience points and undergo a Harrowing deep in the Labyrinth (see E:Ab, p. 148). If a Storyteller allows a deathknight to remove this Flaw with experience, the quest certainly involves a Harrowing and sufficient penance to appease the Malfeans responsible for the deepened curse. The base value of this Flaw assumes the character does not begin play with any permanent Resonance. Characters who actually start with this greater taint add one additional bonus point per dot. Ghosts with this Flaw do not contend with Resonance in any form, but instead, suffer the tainting of their Passions by the Whisper of Oblivion (see E:Ab, p. 284). Such characters receive one bonus point for every dot of tainted Passions they begin play with and must taint all Passions if they lack any rated above one.
cost: 4-pt. Flaw for Abyssals (Abyssals and Ghosts only)
compatibility: RESTRICTED to Abyssals and Ghosts by its own header ("Abyssals and Ghosts only"). This is one of the two Merits/Flaws in this chapter written specifically and primarily for this splat: for Abyssal Exalted, this Flaw grants 4 bonus points (5 if the character starts with permanent Resonance) and converts what would otherwise be a normal Resonance Break (at Resonance >10) into a reset-to-zero-plus-permanent-Resonance-gain instead, capped at the character's Essence. Removable with 5 experience points and a Harrowing deep in the Labyrinth (cross-referenced to this family's own losing-resonance row).
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-death-taint): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. PRIMARY ABYSSAL ROW, the single most Abyssal-specific entry in the entire chapter: this Flaw's own header restricts it to "Abyssals and Ghosts only," and its full mechanical text is a direct modification of this splat's own Resonance system (cross-referenced here to resonance, gaining-resonance, and losing-resonance). Lunar's transcription correctly identified this as "NOT APPLICABLE TO LUNARS" and flagged it for this Abyssal follow-up pass verbatim -- this is that pass. The Ghost-specific Whisper of Oblivion/tainted-Passions variant described in the same paragraph is retained in the mechanics text for completeness (Ghosts can appear as NPCs/antagonists in an Abyssal game) but is not itself an Abyssal PC option.

name: Throwback
summary: An Exalt with this Flaw harbors impulses and personality fragments from a previous incarnation of his Essence, giving his Essence its own distinct Nature. THE SOURCE TEXT EXPLICITLY CARVES OUT A VARIANT FOR ABYSSAL DEATHKNIGHTS: loyal deathknights may harbor an echo of Solar glory pulling them toward Resonance, punishment, and elusive redemption (capped at 3 points); renegade Abyssals actively rebelling against their destiny gain no points for a heroic Throwback but may still profit from a wicked one.
mechanics: An Exalt with this Flaw harbors impulses and personality fragments from a previous incarnation of his Essence. In effect, his Essence has its own different Nature. If the Exalt finds himself in a situation where this Nature would feel strongly and desire a particular course of action, his player must roll Willpower against a difficulty of the Exalt's own Essence rating. If the roll fails, the character acts according to his Essence Nature, but does not regain Willpower for fulfilling its impulses. A botch means the Essence Nature takes over for the rest of the scene, replacing the character's normal personality and pattern of behavior. If a character with this Flaw ever has an Essence rating in excess of his permanent Willpower, his Nature changes entirely to the dictates of the Throwback. The value of this Flaw depends on the degree of deviation and malice of the former self, from a merely inconvenient vestigial personality (one point) up to an outright malignant or insane remnant of a demented god-king (five points). Storytellers may interpolate the two- and four-point versions of this Flaw if so desired. Deathknights loyal to their masters may harbor an echo of Solar glory driving them to Resonance and punishment even as it guides them toward elusive redemption, though such a Throwback is never worth more than three points. Abyssal Exalted actively rebelling against their destiny gain no points for a heroic Throwback but may harbor a wicked personality like other Exalted and profit from it.
cost: Variable point Flaw (1-5, capped at 3 for a loyal deathknight’s Solar-echo variant)
compatibility: RESTRICTED by the Merit/Flaw's own header to "Celestial Exalted only" as written, but the mechanics text explicitly and separately carves out Abyssal deathknights: a LOYAL deathknight may take a Throwback representing an echo of her former Solar glory pulling her toward Resonance, punishment, and elusive redemption, capped at 3 points regardless of severity. A RENEGADE Abyssal actively rebelling against her destiny gains no bonus points for a heroic (redemption-pulling) version of this Flaw, but may still take -- and profit normally from -- a wicked/malignant Throwback at the full 1-5 point range like any other Exalted.
notes: DERIVED FROM LUNAR'S VERIFIED PG TRANSCRIPTION (pg-flaw-throwback): re-cited to the Players Guide directly. INCLUDED DESPITE THE "CELESTIAL EXALTED ONLY" HEADER because the body text explicitly and separately defines two distinct Abyssal variants (loyal deathknight's redemption-pulling echo of Solar glory, capped 3 points; renegade's wicked-personality Throwback, full 1-5 points but no reward for a heroic one) -- Lunar's own transcription flagged this exact header-vs-body inconsistency as directly relevant for this Abyssal follow-up pass. Cross-referenced to this splat's own resonance row since the loyal-deathknight variant explicitly drives the character "to Resonance and punishment."

name: Custom Corpses: Transcendent Revenant Vessel Framework
summary: Chapter Four's core nemissary-crafting framework: how a nemissary (a ghost who has learned the Nemissary's Ride Arcanos) upgrades a possessed corpse into a custom-built "transcendent revenant vessel" rated Artifact one through five, obtained via the Artifact Background (owned outright) or the Backing Background (on loan from a Deathlord), with base stats, decay/repair rules, and a bonus-point pool for the augmentation packages catalogued in the sibling nemissary-vessel-package-* rows.
requirements: For nemissary (ghost) characters only, not the Abyssal deathknight sheet this module covers; the ghost takes the Artifact Background (owned vessel) or the Backing Background (vessel on loan from a Deathlord, revocable at the Deathlord's whim).
mechanics: Any nemissary can possess a common cadaver via the core book's Nemissary's Ride Arcanos, but ghosts favored by an Abyssal Exalt or a Deathlord instead receive a "transcendent revenant vessel": a corpse custom-augmented through necrosurgery, alchemy and necromantic enchantment, ranging from Artifact 1 to 5, never an extra. All versions share Decay Resistance (undamaged while possessed, but every three days of neglect while uninhabited imposes a cumulative -1 die penalty to the nemissary's physical actions, capping at a ten-die penalty that renders the vessel useless) and Enhanced Physique (Strength/Stamina 3, Dexterity/Appearance 2, seven standard mortal health levels, natural soak equal to Stamina; the nemissary may substitute her own higher Attributes but must use the vessel's Appearance and health levels). Vessels do not heal on their own: repairs require a Dexterity + Necrosurgery roll (one success fixes one lethal or two bashing health levels, plus Resources •• in components and one hour per accumulated success), the advanced Instauration of the Fleshly Vessel Arcanos, or the Abyssal Charm Form-Restoring Touch. Modifying a vessel after purchase costs Resources equal to half the augmentation's point value (rounded down), payable to a necrosurgeon or performed by the ghost herself if she knows the Craft. Each vessel receives a bonus-point pool of ([Artifact rating - 1] x 10) points to spend on General Augmentations -- Attributes (4 points/dot, stacking on the base Enhanced Physique numbers, capped at 6 dots), Decay Immunity (5 points, no decay even while uninhabited), Dedicated Attunement (4 points, the vessel resists displacement/exorcism and possession by rival ghosts once bonded via Nemissary's Ride, the Embalmer's Art or later Arcanoi), Hidden Enhancements (6 points, all augmentations function invisibly) -- plus the themed options-package augmentations catalogued in the nemissary-vessel-package-* rows below (The Warm and Pleasing Cadaver, The Corpse Made Stealthy, A Body Built for War).
cost: N/A (framework); individual vessels cost Artifact 1-5, and augmentations cost Resources equal to half their point value, rounded down, on top of the Artifact purchase.
compatibility: Framework/system text supporting the nemissary-vessel-package-* rows below; not itself a directly selectable item on an Abyssal deathknight's sheet.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Nemissaries' and 'Custom Corpses' sections, pp. 87-90 (PDF 88-91), Book of Bone and Ebony. Marked reference-only rather than selectable: although the book explicitly gates vessel acquisition through the standard Artifact/Backing Background purchase mechanism (the same mechanism used for the already-selectable warstrider-class-* rows elsewhere in this inventory), the purchaser here is explicitly "the ghost" (a nemissary), not an Abyssal deathknight -- this Exalted 1e module's Abyssal sheet represents deathknights, who cannot take Nemissary's Ride (it is a ghost-only Arcanos gated by Compassion + Essence, not a Charm gated by Ability + Essence). This mirrors the precedent already set by book-of-bone-and-ebony-chapter-two-arcanoi-excluded for the same reason. The one confirmed player-facing hook is that the altered Followers Background explicitly allows an Abyssal PC to recruit nemissaries as Followers (see followers-background-altered), so this framework remains valuable GM/player reference for statting up a nemissary follower or ally, even though it is not a Background/Artifact purchase the PC's own sheet tracks directly. Flagged for a dedicated review pass on whether a future 'ghost PC' character type would want this promoted to selectable.

name: Nemissary Vessel Package: The Warm and Pleasing Cadaver
summary: One of three themed options packages spendable from a transcendent revenant vessel's bonus-point pool: augmentations for infiltration/diplomacy nemissaries who need to pass convincingly among the living, letting the vessel eat/drink, mimic life signs, or be sculpted to resemble a specific individual.
requirements: Purchased from a transcendent revenant vessel's ([Artifact rating - 1] x 10) bonus-point pool; see custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework.
mechanics: Eat/Drink (5 points): grants a vessel that otherwise cannot hold food or drink enough control to avoid immediately regurgitating two large meals or three small ones before needing to empty its stomach (does not grant digestion). Essence Parasite (10 points): bone-etched enchantments let the ghost drain 1 mote of Essence from any Essence channeler within 10 feet for every two hours of close contact (stacks per channeler present; stacks with Essence-Measuring Thief Arts); usable on mortals instead, at a cost of one unsoakable bashing health level per hour to the mortal. Lifelike (10 points): the vessel shows no outward sign of undeath beyond an ashen or pallid complexion; spending 5 motes for one scene simulates breath, pulse, warmth and basic sexual response well enough that three successes on Perception + Investigation are needed to expose the corpse (any true test of life still succeeds instantly). Sculpted Physiognomy (10 points; buying up Appearance separately is required if the target face exceeds Appearance 3): the vessel's face is surgically remade to resemble a specific individual, foiled only by two successes on a Perception + Investigation roll from someone who knows that individual well.
cost: 5-10 bonus points per augmentation, drawn from the vessel's bonus-point pool; see individual entries above.
compatibility: Requires the custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework's base vessel purchase; stacks freely with the other two options packages and the General Augmentations list.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Options Packages' -> 'The Warm and Pleasing Cadaver' section, p. 89 (PDF 90), Book of Bone and Ebony. Reference-only for the same reason as custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework: this is an a-la-carte menu for building a nemissary (ghost) character or follower, not a purchase an Abyssal deathknight's own sheet makes directly.

name: Nemissary Vessel Package: The Corpse Made Stealthy
summary: One of three themed options packages spendable from a transcendent revenant vessel's bonus-point pool: augmentations for reconnaissance/scout nemissaries, covering speed, evasion of animals and hostile perception, navigation toward the nearest shadowland, and remote sensory transmission back to the Underworld.
requirements: Purchased from a transcendent revenant vessel's ([Artifact rating - 1] x 10) bonus-point pool; see custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework.
mechanics: Built for Speed (5 points): modified leg/pelvic bones let the vessel run at triple its normal running speed indefinitely; spending 5 motes of Essence lets it sprint at full speed for a full day. Repellent to Animals (3 points): a rotten raiton's head sewn into the chest cavity makes ordinary animals avoid the vessel entirely (four/five-dot familiars will approach only if their master's player scores three-plus successes on Manipulation + Presence); costs 2 dice from all the nemissary's Social pools. Repugnant to the Mind's Eye (10 points): ritual scarification and subdermal soulsteel nodules make the vessel psychologically repellent to perceive -- witnesses out of direct, undeniable view suffer -3 successes on Perception rolls to recognize it, and even those looking straight at it in good light suffer a flat -2 dice, their minds reflexively refusing to register what they see. Shadowland Sense (2 points): spending 1 mote and rolling Intelligence + Survival (even a single success suffices) reveals the direction and distance to the nearest shadowland. Transmitting Sense (4 points, purchased separately per sense): for 5 motes, the nemissary streams one sense to a partner in the Underworld carrying a paired amulet, who must also spend 5 motes to receive it (raw sensation only, no narration); the amulet-holder can instead force the link open any time by paying the full 10 motes. Warded against scrying; blocked by anti-scrying wards.
cost: 2-10 bonus points per augmentation, drawn from the vessel's bonus-point pool; see individual entries above.
compatibility: Requires the custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework's base vessel purchase; stacks freely with the other two options packages and the General Augmentations list.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Options Packages' -> 'The Corpse Made Stealthy' section, pp. 89-90 (PDF 90-91), Book of Bone and Ebony. Reference-only for the same reason as custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework.

name: Nemissary Vessel Package: A Body Built for War
summary: One of three themed options packages spendable from a transcendent revenant vessel's bonus-point pool: augmentations for the most common transcendent revenant vessel type, war bodies -- the elite shock-troop officers nemissaries use to direct zombies and hungry ghosts in the Deathlords' assaults on Creation.
requirements: Purchased from a transcendent revenant vessel's ([Artifact rating - 1] x 10) bonus-point pool; see custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework.
mechanics: Armor (2 points per 1L/1B, counts as natural soak rather than worn armor, capped at the vessel's Stamina rating): riveted metal-and-bone plating that caps Appearance at ••; the vessel may only wear armor cut to its own bulky frame. Claws/Blades (4 or 6 points): for 4 points, bone or metal talons grant a Speed +1/Accuracy +1/Damage +1L/Defense +1 (Rate 4 under Exalted Power Combat) slashing attack; for 6 points, forearm-mounted scythe blades instead match the stats of a chosen one-handed sword. Paralytic Touch (4 points): plant-toxin saturation forces a Stamina + Resistance roll (difficulty 2, or 4 if the attack draws blood via claws/fangs) on anyone touched bare-skinned, or be paralyzed for the rest of the scene. Spikes (5 points, caps Appearance at ••): riveted bone/metal spikes add +1L to the vessel's controlled clinch damage while dealing 3L per turn to anyone clinching or crushing it. Stench of Rotting Offal (3 points per purchase, stacking): a revolting brew forces a Stamina + Resistance roll on anyone within 10 feet or they vomit and flee the smell; those who succeed still lose one attack die per purchase of this augmentation from watering eyes. Toughness (4 points per extra -2 health level, 6 points per -1, 8 points per -0): partial mummification, metal reinforcement or grafted extra tissue adds bonus health levels at the chosen severity tier.
cost: 2-8 bonus points per augmentation (per health level/point of soak for Toughness/Armor), drawn from the vessel's bonus-point pool; see individual entries above.
compatibility: Requires the custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework's base vessel purchase; stacks freely with the other two options packages and the General Augmentations list.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Options Packages' -> 'A Body Built for War' section, pp. 90-91 (PDF 91-92), Book of Bone and Ebony. Reference-only for the same reason as custom-corpses-nemissary-vessel-framework; the book itself calls war bodies 'by far the most common type of transcendent revenant vessel,' making this the most frequently used of the three packages when statting nemissary followers or foes.

name: Nemissary Arcanoi and Wonders -- excluded (ghost powers, not Abyssal Charms)
summary: Chapter Four's 'Nemissary Arcanoi and Wonders' section presents four ghost Arcanoi used by nemissaries to maintain and empower their possessed vessels -- Intangible Guardian Presence, The Embalmer's Art (plus its upgrade, the Embalmer's Enduring Triumph), Instauration of the Fleshly Vessel, and Drive the Necrotic Colossus -- all gated by Minimum Compassion + Minimum Essence like every other ghost Arcanos in this book, never by Minimum Ability + Essence like a real player-facing Abyssal Charm.
requirements: N/A -- documents a scope-exclusion finding, not a selectable power.
mechanics: Intangible Guardian Presence (Cost: None; Minimum Compassion 2, Minimum Essence 3; prerequisite Mortal-Shadowing Technique) is an Ox-Body-Charm analog that fortifies only a vessel the ghost is currently riding, purchasable up to the ghost's Compassion rating. The Embalmer's Art (15 motes committed, 2 Willpower; Minimum Compassion 2, Minimum Essence 3; prerequisite Nemissary's Ride) grants automatic, rollless possession via Nemissary's Ride, halts the vessel's decay for the duration, and lets the ghost spend 4 motes per -2 health level (up to her Compassion) to fortify it; its upgrade, the Embalmer's Enduring Triumph (Minimum Compassion 3, Minimum Essence 4, prerequisite the Embalmer's Art), does the same for 10 motes/1 Willpower plus 2 motes per -1 health level, waiving the Willpower cost in a shadowland. Instauration of the Fleshly Vessel (Cost varies; Minimum Compassion 3, Minimum Essence 4; prerequisite the Embalmer's Art) repairs rot (4 motes undoes one day's accumulated rot damage) or heals combat damage to the vessel at the cost of the ghost's own corpus (1 mote per health level healed, at 1 unsoakable level of matching damage to the ghost per level restored); it cannot mend fire, aggravated, or anti-undead-specific damage. Drive the Necrotic Colossus (10 motes, 1 Willpower, 1 experience point; Minimum Compassion 2, Minimum Essence 4; prerequisite Nemissary's Ride) lets a ghost animate/pilot shells larger than a very large human, up to temple-sized war machines, with multiple nemissaries needed in concert for anything bigger; spending the experience point removes the ongoing Essence commitment. This is the Charm the 30 nemissaries piloting the Mask of Winters' Juggernaut use.
compatibility: Ghost (nemissary) character powers only; not available to Abyssal deathknights.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Nemissary Arcanoi and Wonders' section, pp. 91-92 (PDF 92-93), Book of Bone and Ebony. Excluded per the exact precedent already set by book-of-bone-and-ebony-chapter-two-arcanoi-excluded: every Charm-like ability here is a ghost Arcanos gated by Minimum Virtue (Compassion) + Essence, not a Minimum Ability + Essence Abyssal Charm, so none of it is selectable on a deathknight's sheet. Documented as one chapter-section-level excluded row rather than four separate Arcanos rows, matching that same precedent's granularity. Drive the Necrotic Colossus is cross-referenced from the war-machine-construction-framework row's Animation Options (Nemissaries) subsection, since it is the mechanism nemissary-piloted war machines actually use.

name: Bindings of Eternal Preservation (Resources •• or •••)
summary: Linen or leather wrappings soaked in mummification chemicals that halt (but do not reverse) a corpse's decay for as long as they stay wrapped, sold at two tiers of durability and available to any character with the Resources rating to buy them -- including for use on a size class 3 or 4 war machine, at extra cost.
requirements: Resources •• (cloth) or Resources ••• (leather).
mechanics: The wrappings must cover the corpse with no more than an inch of exposed tissue between bindings to be effective; they halt further decay but do not reverse decay already present. Cloth bindings (Resources ••) are cheaper but last only one year, are unsuited to combat use, and sever in two places per level of lethal damage taken (requiring two turns to retie each time, or the wrappings fall off after 10 cumulative lethal levels, ruining them). Leather bindings (Resources •••) require a much longer preparation soak but last up to a century, add 2L/1B to the wearer's soak, and only need retying if the wearer suffers aggravated damage. Zombies tend to shred either kind within hours. Applying bindings to a war machine is possible but costly: the Resources cost increases by • for a size class 3 war machine and by •• for a size class 4 war machine.
cost: Resources •• (cloth, lasts one year) or Resources ••• (leather, lasts up to a century); +• Resources for a size class 3 war machine, +•• for size class 4.
compatibility: Usable on any corpse, nemissary vessel, or war machine frame; does not reverse existing decay, only halts further decay.
notes: Chapter Four: Creations of Bone, 'Bindings of Eternal Preservation' section, pp. 92-93 (PDF 93-94), Book of Bone and Ebony. Marked selectable (unlike the ghost-only Arcanoi/vessel rows above) because this is a plain Resources-rated purchasable item, matching the precedent set by stomach-weighting-powder and other Resources-rated catalog entries elsewhere in this inventory -- any character (Abyssal, mortal ally, or nemissary) with the requisite Resources dots can buy it.

name: War Machine Construction Framework (Frame, Size Class, Weapon Mounts, Passengers, Animation, Defense and Offense)
