Steelsilk adds +1 to all Sail rolls for control during a storm or for gaining or losing speed, and lets a ship sail two points closer to the wind; the sails are all but impenetrable by mundane weapons (a ballista might punch a hole in one, but sails made of steelsilk have 15B/10L soak, take 20 health levels to damage and 40 to destroy) and take only half damage from wind, waves, and fire. Repairing steelsilk sails requires a Charm or Crack-Mending Technique; no other way is known today to mend steelsilk once it is damaged.
compatibility: Any ship owner or captain, of any splat including Abyssals; no splat restriction stated in the source text.
notes: Chapter Four: Creatures, Gods, Charms and Artifacts, 'Artifacts of the Waves', 'Steelsilk Sails (Artifact ••)', printed p. 124 (PDF 125), Savage Seas. Transcribed directly from the rendered source PDF (image-based, no selectable text layer). Universal item, no splat-restricting text; selectable for Abyssal without qualification.

name: Storm Sapphire (Artifact ••• for lesser stones or •••• for the black stones)
summary: Giant enchanted sapphires, most the size of a man's fist or larger, that let an Exalted quell a storm by feeding it motes of Essence, Willpower, and health levels drawn from her own life force; power and cost scale with the color of the stone and the storm's ferocity.
requirements: An Essence-manipulating wielder (Exalted, spirit, or god-blooded) able to power the sapphire with Essence, Willpower, and health levels.
mechanics: Storm sapphires are giant sapphires, most the size of a man's fist or larger. The most powerful storm sapphires are black, but they come in all colors, with green sapphires (the least powerful) being the most common. Common storm sapphires have the power to quell storms, calming the sea and sky even under the most savage conditions, but this power does not come without a cost: to stop a storm, an Exalted must power the sapphire with her own life force, paying motes of Essence, Willpower, and health levels per the Storm Sapphire Effect Table (below); these health levels cannot be soaked or reduced if the stone is to work properly, though they heal normally afterward. The user can attempt to judge how strong an incoming storm will be with a Perception + Occult roll (difficulty starts at 2, ranging up to 5 for an extremely fast-moving, powerful, unforeseen storm) before trying to stop it. Magically summoned or influenced storms are easier to predict and control: reduce the storm's severity by one level for purposes of determining dissipation cost, and reduce the judging difficulty by 2 (minimum difficulty 2). Lesser stones (green through light blue) can disperse most storms but can do nothing against the strongest ones -- a storm sapphire's power either works outright or does not; the darkest blue and black stones can disperse any storm, but the cost in life force scales with the storm's ferocity, and the wielder will not know in advance how much of her existence she must devote before choosing to battle it. STORM SAPPHIRE EFFECT TABLE (Storm Strength / Cost for Blue or Green Sapphire / Cost for Black Sapphire): Storm: 20 motes, 2 Willpower, 2 health levels / 20 motes, 2 Willpower, 2 health levels. Greater storm: 25 motes, 2 Willpower, 3 health levels / 25 motes, 2 Willpower, 2 health levels. Gale: 25 motes, 3 Willpower, 3 health levels / 25 motes, 3 Willpower, 2 health levels. Greater gale: 30 motes, 4 Willpower, 3 health levels / 25 motes, 3 Willpower, 3 health levels. Hurricane: cannot be quelled / 30 motes, 4 Willpower, 3 health levels. Greater hurricane: cannot be quelled / 35 motes, 4 Willpower, 4 health levels. Tsunami: cannot be quelled / 40 motes, 5 Willpower, 4 health levels. Greater tsunami: cannot be quelled / 45 motes, 5 Willpower, 5 health levels. Island killer: cannot be quelled / 50 motes, 6 Willpower, 6 health levels. A character who lacks sufficient motes or Willpower can, for the sapphire's purposes only, convert health levels into motes or Willpower (one health level = 10 motes of Essence or 1 Willpower); this may only be done if the user lacks sufficient resources otherwise, and cannot be used to leave himself with no motes after the storm dissipates. Creating a storm sapphire involves the sapphire itself (utterly without flaw), the blood of a Storm Mother, and a wind spirit that has never seen a mortal before being captured; the enchantment takes a year and a day and must be performed on a ship floating in the clear waters of the uttermost West, out of sight of any land, which is why so few exist. Storytellers are encouraged NOT to use this artifact to slay out of hand any player character who tries to stop a major storm without compelling reason; only the greatest storms (the ones of legend) are sufficient to kill a Terrestrial Exalted, and even those cannot withstand the might of a Solar focused through a storm sapphire -- draining the Exalted of six motes of Essence or Willpower plus six health levels is more appropriate than killing the character in general, though Storyteller characters sacrificing themselves to save the player characters are a separate, valid dramatic option.
cost: See the Storm Sapphire Effect Table in mechanics: 20-50 motes plus 2-6 Willpower plus 2-6 health levels, scaled to storm strength and stone color; black stones can quell any storm, lesser (green through light blue) stones cannot affect the strongest storms at any cost.
compatibility: Any Essence-manipulating wielder (Exalted, spirit, or god-blooded), of any splat including Abyssals; prized and sought after by Exalted sea captains and fleet admirals, few exist due to the difficulty and rarity of their creation ritual.
notes: Chapter Four: Creatures, Gods, Charms and Artifacts, 'Artifacts of the Waves', 'Storm Sapphire (Artifact ••• for lesser stones or •••• for the black stones)', printed pp. 124-125 (PDF 125-126), Savage Seas, including the 'Storm Sapphire Effect Table' (printed p. 125/PDF 126). Transcribed directly from a zoomed, upscaled re-crop of the rendered source PDF table (image-based, no selectable text layer) to confirm exact figures per row/column. Universal item, no splat-restricting text; selectable for Abyssal without qualification.

name: Cord of Winds (Artifact •)
summary: A relatively common silken cord tied with a number of knots, each binding a minor air elemental that will serve for a day and a night raising wind when released and asked; larger, more complex knots bind more powerful elementals.
requirements: None to use; any character may release a bound elemental by untying its knot, though unraveling a knot in a hurry requires an extended Wits + Sail roll.
mechanics: A relatively common artifact, produced by even mortal sorcerers. Partially discharged examples can be found on many ships, even relatively small ones, as they have been created in large numbers over the centuries. The cord of winds is normally a silken cord, usually light blue but possibly of any color, adorned with a number of knots. Each knot holds a minor air elemental bound in it; if released, an elemental will serve for a day and a night, raising wind when asked. After its service is up, the elemental is free to depart. Any attempt to detain the elemental will be poorly received and may well bring retribution down upon the offending party at some point. Most cords will have 20 knots in them when first created, of different sizes and complexities; the smaller, simpler knots hold elementals that are little more than breezes, while the elementals bound in the larger, more complex knots are more powerful. Unraveling a knot in a hurry is an extended Wits + Sail task; the difficulty depends on the power of the air elemental bound up in the knot -- a simple breeze's knot has a difficulty of 4, while the knot securing a powerful zephyr or gale might have a difficulty of 10, though such powerful elementals or spirits are only rarely bound in a cord of winds (most elementals or spirits bound will have a permanent Essence less than 4). Any knot can be untied given enough time, if one is patient enough, or cut in half.
compatibility: Any user, mortal or Exalted, of any splat including Abyssals; produced even by mortal sorcerers, no splat restriction stated in the source text.
notes: Chapter Four: Creatures, Gods, Charms and Artifacts, 'Artifacts of the Waves', 'Cord of Winds (Artifact •)', printed pp. 125-126 (PDF 126-127), Savage Seas. Transcribed directly from the rendered source PDF (image-based, no selectable text layer). Universal item, no splat-restricting text; selectable for Abyssal without qualification.

name: Wavecleaver Daiklaive (Artifact ••)
summary: An uncommon, unusually short daiklave (rarely exceeding three feet of blade) built for fighting belowdecks in cramped quarters and low ceilings, wielded mostly by House V'neef and House Peleps Terrestrials but found in small numbers among most houses.
requirements: Minimum Strength •• to wield effectively.
mechanics: Speed +3, Accuracy +2, Damage +5L, Defense +1, Minimum Strength ••. Wavecleavers are uncommon weapons, wielded mostly by Terrestrials of House V'neef and House Peleps, although most houses have a small number of them. Perhaps the shortest of daiklaives, rarely exceeding three feet in blade length, wavecleavers are perfect for work belowdecks, where cramped quarters and low ceilings are the norm. Their thick blades and strong edges make them useful as tools as well as weapons; even steel cables or chains will rarely withstand more than a single hack from the curved blade of a wavecleaver. Wavecleavers typically have sockets for two Hearthstones, as Exalted on the water are more likely to rely on the gem-like talismans for survival.
compatibility: Any daiklave-capable wielder meeting the Minimum Strength requirement, of any splat including Abyssals; most common among House V'neef and House Peleps Dragon-Blooded, but most Great Houses keep a small number, with no splat restriction stated in the source text.
notes: Chapter Four: Creatures, Gods, Charms and Artifacts, 'Artifacts of the Waves', 'Wavecleaver Daiklaive (Artifact ••)', printed p. 126 (PDF 127), Savage Seas. Transcribed directly from the rendered source PDF (image-based, no selectable text layer). Universal item, no splat-restricting text; selectable for Abyssal without qualification.

name: Light Implosion Bow (Artifact ••, ••• if Hearthstone or reagent powered)
summary: A First Age ship-mounted ballista-like weapon of dark wine-red wood inlaid with the Five Magical Materials that any Essence-channeling wielder can fire to launch adjustable-damage bolts of pure Essence, useful against rigging, troops, or units alike.
requirements: Any Exalted type, Fair Folk, or other Essence-channeler to fire; characters unable to channel Essence cannot operate these artifacts. A character without prior experience must succeed on an Intelligence + Lore roll at difficulty 3 to decipher the controls.
mechanics: Accuracy +3, Range 500, Rate 1; Naval Range Long, Naval Rate 3/turn, Minimum None, Artifact •• or •••. These fearsome weapons are First Age relics whose full workings remain beyond the understanding of any savant or engineer of the present day, though their use is simple once the operator becomes familiar with their functioning. Resembling a ballista mounted atop a heavy gimbaled pedestal, these mechanisms appear to be made of a dark, glossy, wine-red wood, with elaborate inlays and fittings of the Five Magical Materials. When properly used by a character capable of channeling Essence (any Exalted type and also Fair Folk and possibly others), these weapons launch projectiles of pure Essence, fired using Archery. Before firing, the user selects the type of damage to be done, and the amount depends on how many motes of Essence the user channels into the weapon: for 1 mote, the projectile inflicts either 7B or 5L damage (depending on control settings) on everything within a 10-foot radius of its target -- in naval combat, these settings allow attacks against rigging with the weapon, and it can also be used against units or troops; for 2 motes, the range and area of effect remain the same, but the damage settings increase to 15B or 12L. The weapon's pedestal must be mounted securely to a solid surface to fire; the bow has an arc of fire extending 360 degrees horizontally and 90 degrees vertically (30 degrees below and 60 above horizontal). Some versions are powered by Hearthstones, and some by alchemical reagents; typically, however, they are manned by one of the Dragon-Blooded, who powers it with his own Essence. Light implosion bows are less demanding to maintain than the more powerful lightning ballista, but an implosion bow must still be serviced every 100 shots by a character with Lore ••• and Occult ••; the overhaul includes replacement/repair of small mechanism parts made of exotic and rare components, and costs Resources ••••, components unlikely to be found outside the Realm and the largest Threshold cities.
cost: 1 mote per shot (7B/5L damage, 10-foot radius) or 2 motes per shot (15B/12L damage, same radius); Resources •••• plus Lore ••• and Occult •• every 100 shots for servicing.
compatibility: Any Essence-channeling wielder (any Exalted type, Fair Folk, and possibly others, including Abyssals); characters unable to channel Essence cannot operate these artifacts. Commonly mounted on First Age warships and manned by a Dragon-Blooded crewmember, but no splat restriction is stated for who may fire one.

name: Lightning Ballista (Artifact ••• for a common version, •••• for a Hearthstone or elemental powered version)
summary: The primary heavy armament of larger First Age warships: a complex brass-and-silver ship-mounted weapon that releases a scorching blast of lightning capable of damaging even the heaviest hulls, powered by the crew's own Essence, a bound air elemental, or a Hearthstone of Fire or Air.
requirements: Only an Exalted (or otherwise Essence-manipulating) firer can activate one; lightning ballistae are powerless in the hands of the unExalted. Archery Charms cannot be used to enhance its operation.
mechanics: Lightning ballistae made up the primary heavy armament of larger First Age warships, with implosion bows and other weapons acting as secondary devices. Powerful, although shorter ranged than some other devices known to have existed, lightning ballistae are capable of damaging even the heaviest First Age hulls, and the few still in service are carefully guarded. When fired, the lightning ballista releases a powerful blast of lightning that sears and scorches whatever it hits, instantly burning wood and flesh to ash and melting steel or stone. Lightning ballistae are heavy and complex affairs, built largely of brass and silver, and require complex fuels and reagents in the institution of Essence to fire; typically, a lightning ballista must be fueled by up to twenty shots before servicing and maintenance. Maintaining a lightning ballista requires a character with Lore •••• and Occult •••• to keep the weapon properly tuned and charged; parts for maintenance normally cost Resources •••• every 100 firings, and the fuels/reagents used cost Resources ••• for 20 shots -- materials difficult but not impossible to find outside a large city. Lightning ballistae are commonly mounted centerline on the hull just aft of the prow, on a swivel mount allowing the muzzle to fire on a 270-degree arc, with a traverse of 45 degrees (15 down, 30 up). Only a small number of ships carried more than one, and few have survived to the current day. The most common were powered by the Exalted crew, though examples exist that were powered by captured (or willing) air elementals or through the use of an Essence stone. Lightning ballistae powered purely by Essence require 3 motes per shot; those that bind elementals use 1 of the elemental's motes and 1 of the firer's motes; those powered by Hearthstones require a Hearthstone of Fire or a Hearthstone of Air (Manse •• or above) to function. All lightning ballistae are designed so the firer must be able to manipulate Essence to activate them. Although fired using the Archery Ability, Archery Charms cannot be used to enhance the operation of a lightning ballista. Lightning Ballista (elemental) +2/20L/1/1,000/Very Long/3 per turn/Occult •••, Archery •/••••. Lightning Ballista (Hearthstone) +2/25L/--/1,000/Very Long/2 per turn/Occult ••, Archery •/••••.
cost: 3 motes per shot (purely Essence-powered); 1 of the firer's motes plus 1 of a bound elemental's motes (elemental-powered); a Hearthstone of Fire or Air rated Manse •• or above (Hearthstone-powered, no per-shot mote cost); plus Resources •••• per 100 firings and Resources ••• per 20 shots of fuel/reagents for upkeep.
compatibility: Any Exalted or otherwise Essence-manipulating firer, of any splat including Abyssals; the weapon itself is powerless in unExalted hands. Mounted on larger First Age warships, carefully guarded by whoever still holds a surviving example.
